अथापश्यत्क्षणेनैव प्रेतसंघैः सभावृतम् ..
प्रेतमेकं च सर्वेषामाधिपत्ये व्यव स्थितम् .. 23 ..
5.65.m: Then in that very moment he saw an assembly surrounded by multitudes of pretas, / and one preta established in authority over all of them.

5.65.s:
tataste pārśvagāḥ pretā eke nṛtyaṃ pracakrire ..
tatpuro gītamanye tu stutiṃ caiva tathā pare .. 24 ..
5.65.d:
ततस्ते पार्श्वगाः प्रेता एके नृत्यं प्रचक्रिरे ..
तत्पुरो गीतमन्ये तु स्तुतिं चैव तथा परे .. 24 ..
5.65.m: Then those pretas standing at his side—some performed a dance / before him, while others [sang] a song, and still others [uttered] praise.

5.65.s:
athāsau prāha taṃ śūdramatithe kuru bhojanam ..
svecchayā piba toyaṃ ca śreyo yena bhavenmama .. 25 ..
5.65.d:
अथासौ प्राह तं शूद्रमतिथे कुरु भोजनम् ..
स्वेच्छया पिब तोयं च श्रेयो येन भवेन्मम .. 25 ..
5.65.m: Then he said to that Śūdra: “O guest, take your meal; / and drink water at will, so that welfare may come to me.”

5.65.s:
tataḥ sa bhojanaṃ cakre kṣudhārtaśca papau jalam ..
bhayaṃ tyaktvā suviśrabdhaḥ pretarājasya śāsanāt .. 26 ..
5.65.d:
ततः स भोजनं चक्रे क्षुधार्तश्च पपौ जलम् ..
भयं त्यक्त्वा सुविश्रब्धः प्रेतराजस्य शासनात् .. 26 ..
5.65.m: Then, tormented by hunger, he ate food and drank water, / casting off fear and becoming fully confident at the command of the king of pretas.

5.65.s:
tataḥ pretāśca te sarve pretatvena samanvitāḥ ..
yathājyeṣṭhaṃ yathānyāyaṃ pracakrurbhojanakriyām..27..
5.65.d:
ततः प्रेताश्च ते सर्वे प्रेतत्वेन समन्विताः ..
यथाज्येष्ठं यथान्यायं प्रचक्रुर्भोजनक्रियाम्..27..
5.65.m: Then all those pretas, endowed with the condition of pretas, / carried out the act of dining according to seniority and proper custom.

5.65.s:
evaṃ teṣāṃ samastānāṃ vilāsaiḥ pārthivocitaiḥ ..
atikrāntā niśā sarvā krīḍatāṃ dvijasattamāḥ .. 28 ..
5.65.d:
एवं तेषां समस्तानां विलासैः पार्थिवोचितैः ..
अतिक्रान्ता निशा सर्वा क्रीडतां द्विजसत्तमाः .. 28 ..
5.65.m: Thus, with amusements fit for monarchs, the entire night / passed for all of them while they sported, O best of brahmins.

5.65.s:
tataḥ prabhāte vimale prodgate ravimaṃḍale ..
yāvatpaśyati śūdraḥ sa tāvattatra na kiñcana .. 29 ..
5.65.d:
ततः प्रभाते विमले प्रोद्गते रविमंडले ..
यावत्पश्यति शूद्रः स तावत्तत्र न किञ्चन .. 29 ..
5.65.m: Then, at pure dawn when the sun's disc had risen, / as far as that Śūdra looked, there was nothing whatsoever there.

5.65.s:
tataśca cintayāmāsa kimetatsvapnadarśanam ..
cittabhramo'thavā'smākamindrajālamathāpi vā .. 6.65.30 ..
athavā satyametaddhi yato me tṛptiruttamā ..
saṃjāteyaṃ kṣudhārttasya pipāsākulitasya ca ..3...
5.65.d:
ततश्च चिन्तयामास किमेतत्स्वप्नदर्शनम् ..
चित्तभ्रमोऽथवाऽस्माकमिन्द्रजालमथापि वा .. 6.65.30 ..
अथवा सत्यमेतद्धि यतो मे तृप्तिरुत्तमा ..
संजातेयं क्षुधार्त्तस्य पिपासाकुलितस्य च ..3...
5.65.m:
Then he pondered: “What was this vision of a dream? / Or is it a delusion of my mind, or perhaps an illusion?
Or rather, it must indeed be real, since this supreme satisfaction / arose in me, who was afflicted by hunger and agitated by thirst.”

5.65.s:
evaṃ cintayamānasya bhāskaro gaganāṃgaṇam ..
samāruroha tāpena tāpayandharaṇītalam .. 32 ..
5.65.d:
एवं चिन्तयमानस्य भास्करो गगनांगणम् ..
समारुरोह तापेन तापयन्धरणीतलम् .. 32 ..
5.65.m: While he was thus reflecting, the sun mounted the courtyard of the sky, / scorching the surface of the earth with its heat.

5.65.s:
tataḥ kaṃcitsamāśritya svalpacchāyaṃ mahīruham ..
prāptavāndivasasyāṃtaṃ kṣutpipāsāprapīḍitaḥ .. 33 ..
5.65.d:
ततः कंचित्समाश्रित्य स्वल्पच्छायं महीरुहम् ..
प्राप्तवान्दिवसस्यांतं क्षुत्पिपासाप्रपीडितः .. 33 ..
5.65.m: Then, having taken shelter under a tree with meager shade, / he reached the end of the day, sorely afflicted by hunger and thirst.

5.65.s:
tato niśāmukhe prāpte bhūyo'pi pretarājakam ..
pretaistaiścasamopetaṃ tathārūpaṃ vyalokayat .. 34 ..
5.65.d:
ततो निशामुखे प्राप्ते भूयोऽपि प्रेतराजकम् ..
प्रेतैस्तैश्चसमोपेतं तथारूपं व्यलोकयत् .. 34 ..
5.65.m: Then, when nightfall arrived, he again beheld that king of pretas / accompanied by those pretas, having that same appearance.

5.65.s:
tathaiva bhojanaṃ cakre tasyātithyasamudbhavam ..
bhayena rahitaḥ śūdro harṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ .. 35 ..
5.65.d:
तथैव भोजनं चक्रे तस्यातिथ्यसमुद्भवम् ..
भयेन रहितः शूद्रो हर्षेण महतान्वितः .. 35 ..
5.65.m: In the same manner, free from fear and filled with great joy, / the Śūdra took the meal arising from his hospitality.

5.65.s:
evaṃ tasya niśāvaktre nityameva sa bhūpatiḥ ..
ātithyaṃ prakarotyeva samāgatya tathaiva ca .. 36 ..
5.65.d:
एवं तस्य निशावक्त्रे नित्यमेव स भूपतिः ..
आतिथ्यं प्रकरोत्येव समागत्य तथैव च .. 36 ..
5.65.m: Thus, at the onset of night, that king constantly arrived / and offered hospitality to him in that very way.

5.65.s:
tato'nyadivase prāpte tena śūdreṇa bhūpatiḥ ..
pṛṣṭaḥ kimetadāścaryaṃ dṛśyate rajanīmukhe .. 37 ..
5.65.d:
ततोऽन्यदिवसे प्राप्ते तेन शूद्रेण भूपतिः ..
पृष्टः किमेतदाश्चर्यं दृश्यते रजनीमुखे .. 37 ..
5.65.m: Then, when another day arrived, the king was asked by that Śūdra: / “What is this marvel seen at the onset of night?

5.65.s:
vibhavaste mahābhāga praṇaśyati niśākṣaye ..
etatkīrtaya me guhyaṃ na cetpretapa saṃsthitam ..
atra kautūhalaṃ jātaṃ dṛṣṭvedaṃ suviceṣṭitam .. 38 ..
5.65.d:
विभवस्ते महाभाग प्रणश्यति निशाक्षये ..
एतत्कीर्तय मे गुह्यं न चेत्प्रेतप संस्थितम् ..
अत्र कौतूहलं जातं दृष्ट्वेदं सुविचेष्टितम् .. 38 ..
5.65.m: Your wealth and power, O fortunate one, vanishes at the end of the night. / Tell me this secret, unless it is forbidden, O lord of pretas! / Curiosity has arisen in me having seen this remarkable affair.”

5.65.s:
.. preta uvāca .. ..
asti puṇyaṃ mahākṣetraṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñitam ..
gaṃgā ca yamunā caiva sthite tatra ca saṃgame .. 39 ..
5.65.d:
.. प्रेत उवाच .. ..
अस्ति पुण्यं महाक्षेत्रं हाटकेश्वरसंज्ञितम् ..
गंगा च यमुना चैव स्थिते तत्र च संगमे .. 39 ..
5.65.m: The preta said: / “There is a holy, great sacred field called Hāṭakeśvara; / both the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā are situated there at their confluence.

5.65.s:
tābhyāmatisamīpasthaṃ śivasyāyatanaṃ śubham ..
mahāvratadharastatra tapasyati sunaiṣṭhikaḥ .. 6.65.40 ..
5.65.d:
ताभ्यामतिसमीपस्थं शिवस्यायतनं शुभम् ..
महाव्रतधरस्तत्र तपस्यति सुनैष्ठिकः .. 6.65.40 ..
5.65.m: Very close to both of them is an auspicious abode of Śiva; / there, a deeply devout ascetic observing the great vow performs austerities.

5.65.s:
sa sadā rātriśaucārthaṃ kapālaṃ jalapūritam ..
madīyaṃ śayane cakre tatra kṛtvā nijāṃ kriyām .. 41 ..
5.65.d:
स सदा रात्रिशौचार्थं कपालं जलपूरितम् ..
मदीयं शयने चक्रे तत्र कृत्वा निजां क्रियाम् .. 41 ..
5.65.m: For night-time purification, having performed his rite there, / he always places by his bed a skull filled with water, which is mine.

5.65.s:
tatprabhāvānmameyaṃ hi vibhūtirjāyate niśi ..
divā rikte kṛte yāti bhūya eva mahāmate..42..
5.65.d:
तत्प्रभावान्ममेयं हि विभूतिर्जायते निशि ..
दिवा रिक्ते कृते याति भूय एव महामते..42..
5.65.m: By the power of that, indeed, this fortune of mine arises at night; / but when it is made empty by day, it departs again, O intelligent one.

5.65.s:
tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me tatra gatvā kapālakam ..
cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā madīyaṃ tattasmiṃstoye vinikṣipa ..43..
5.65.d:
तस्मात्कुरु प्रसादं मे तत्र गत्वा कपालकम् ..
चूर्णं कृत्वा मदीयं तत्तस्मिंस्तोये विनिक्षिप ..43..
5.65.m: Therefore, do me a favor: go there, / grind that skull of mine into powder, and throw it into that water,

5.65.s: yena me jāyate mokṣaḥ pretabhāvātsudāruṇāt .. 44 ..
5.65.d: येन मे जायते मोक्षः प्रेतभावात्सुदारुणात् .. 44 ..
5.65.m: so that liberation may come to me from the terrible condition of a preta.

5.65.s:
tathā tatrāsti pūrvasyāṃ diśi tattīrthamuttamam ..
gayāśira iti khyātaṃ pretatvānmuktidā yakam .. 45 ..
5.65.d:
तथा तत्रास्ति पूर्वस्यां दिशि तत्तीर्थमुत्तमम् ..
गयाशिर इति ख्यातं प्रेतत्वान्मुक्तिदा यकम् .. 45 ..
5.65.m: Likewise, in the eastern quarter there is that supreme sacred ford / known as Gayāśiras, which bestows liberation from the state of a preta.

5.65.s:
tatra gatvā kuru śrāddhaṃ sarveṣāṃ tvaṃ mahāmate ..
dṛśyate tava pārśvasthā bhadra saṃpuṭikā śubhām .. 46 ..
5.65.d:
तत्र गत्वा कुरु श्राद्धं सर्वेषां त्वं महामते ..
दृश्यते तव पार्श्वस्था भद्र संपुटिका शुभाम् .. 46 ..
5.65.m: Go there and perform a śrāddha for all of us, O intelligent one; / seen at your side, good sir, is an auspicious casket.

5.65.s:
asyāṃ nāmāni sarveṣāṃ yathājyeṣṭhaṃ samālikha ..
tataḥ śrāddhaṃ kuruṣvāśu dayāṃ kṛtvā garīyasīm .. 47 ..
5.65.d:
अस्यां नामानि सर्वेषां यथाज्येष्ठं समालिख ..
ततः श्राद्धं कुरुष्वाशु दयां कृत्वा गरीयसीम् .. 47 ..
5.65.m: Write down the names of all upon this, in order of seniority; / then quickly perform the śrāddha, having shown great compassion.

5.65.s:
vayaṃ tvāṃ tatra neṣyāmaḥ sukhopāyena bhadraka..
nidhiṃ ca darśayiṣyāmaḥ śrāddhārthaṃ sumahattaram .. 48 ..
5.65.d:
वयं त्वां तत्र नेष्यामः सुखोपायेन भद्रक..
निधिं च दर्शयिष्यामः श्राद्धार्थं सुमहत्तरम् .. 48 ..
5.65.m: We shall carry you there by an easy means, good sir, / and we shall reveal a very great treasure for the sake of the śrāddha.”

5.65.s:
tatheti samanujñāte tena śūdreṇa satvaram ..
ninyustaṃ skandhamāropya śūdraṃ kṣetre yathoditam .. 49 ..
5.65.d:
तथेति समनुज्ञाते तेन शूद्रेण सत्वरम् ..
निन्युस्तं स्कन्धमारोप्य शूद्रं क्षेत्रे यथोदितम् .. 49 ..
5.65.m: When it was assented to with 'So be it' by that Śūdra, / they quickly lifted the Śūdra upon their shoulders and brought him to the sacred field as mentioned.

5.65.s:
darśayāmāsurevāsya nidhānaṃ bhūrivittajam ..
tadādāya gatastatra yatrāsau naiṣṭhikaḥ sthitaḥ .. 6.65.50 ..
5.65.d:
दर्शयामासुरेवास्य निधानं भूरिवित्तजम् ..
तदादाय गतस्तत्र यत्रासौ नैष्ठिकः स्थितः .. 6.65.50 ..
5.65.m: They showed him a hoard yielding abundant wealth; / taking it, he went to where that perpetual ascetic was staying.

5.65.s:
tataḥ praṇamya taṃ bhaktyā katha yāmāsa vistarāt ..
tasya bhūtapateḥ sarvaṃ vṛttāṃtaṃ vinayānvitaḥ .. 51 ..
5.65.d:
ततः प्रणम्य तं भक्त्या कथ यामास विस्तरात् ..
तस्य भूतपतेः सर्वं वृत्तांतं विनयान्वितः .. 51 ..
5.65.m: Then, bowing to him with devotion, endowed with humility, / he related in full detail the entire story of that lord of spirits.

5.65.s:
tato labdhvā kapālaṃ taccūrṇayitvā samāhitaḥ ..
gaṃgāyamunayormadhye pracikṣepa mudānvitaḥ .. 52 ..
5.65.d:
ततो लब्ध्वा कपालं तच्चूर्णयित्वा समाहितः ..
गंगायमुनयोर्मध्ये प्रचिक्षेप मुदान्वितः .. 52 ..
5.65.m: Then, having obtained that skull and ground it to powder with focused mind, / he cast it with joy into the midst of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā.

5.65.s:
etasminnaṃtare preto divyarūpavapurdharaḥ ..
vimānastho'bravīdvākyaṃ śūdraṃ taṃ harṣasaṃyutaḥ .. 53 ..
5.65.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्रेतो दिव्यरूपवपुर्धरः ..
विमानस्थोऽब्रवीद्वाक्यं शूद्रं तं हर्षसंयुतः .. 53 ..
5.65.m: In the meantime, the ghost, assuming a divine form and body, / seated in an aerial chariot, spoke these words to that śūdra, filled with joy:

5.65.s:
prasādāttava mukto'haṃ pretatvāddāruṇāditaḥ ..
svasti te'stu gamiṣyāmi sāṃprataṃ tridivālayam .. 54 ..
5.65.d:
प्रसादात्तव मुक्तोऽहं प्रेतत्वाद्दारुणादितः ..
स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि सांप्रतं त्रिदिवालयम् .. 54 ..
5.65.m: "By your grace I have been freed from this dreadful condition of a ghost. / May all be well with you; I shall now go to the abode of heaven.

5.65.s:
eteṣāmeva sarveṣāmidānīṃ śrāddhamācara ..
gatvā gayāśiraḥ puṇyaṃ yena muktiḥ prajāyate .. 55 ..
5.65.d:
एतेषामेव सर्वेषामिदानीं श्राद्धमाचर ..
गत्वा गयाशिरः पुण्यं येन मुक्तिः प्रजायते .. 55 ..
5.65.m: Perform now the ancestral rites for all these others as well, / having gone to holy Gayāśiras, whereby liberation is attained."

5.65.s:
tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭasteṣāmeva pṛthakpṛthak ..
śrāddhaṃ cakre ca bhūtānāṃ nityameva samāhitaḥ .. 56 ..
5.65.d:
ततः स विस्मयाविष्टस्तेषामेव पृथक्पृथक् ..
श्राद्धं चक्रे च भूतानां नित्यमेव समाहितः .. 56 ..
5.65.m: Then, filled with wonder, he performed the ancestral rites / for each of those spirits individually, ever concentrated in mind.

5.65.s:
te'pi sarve gatāḥ svargaṃ pretāstasya prabhāvataḥ ..
daduśca darśanaṃ tasya svapre harṣasamanvitāḥ .. 57 ..
5.65.d:
तेऽपि सर्वे गताः स्वर्गं प्रेतास्तस्य प्रभावतः ..
ददुश्च दर्शनं तस्य स्वप्रे हर्षसमन्विताः .. 57 ..
5.65.m: By his power, all those ghosts also went to heaven, / and, filled with joy, they appeared to him in a dream.

5.65.s:
tataḥ śūdraḥ sa vijñāya tatkṣetraṃ puṇyavardha nam ..
na jagāma gṛhaṃ bhūyastatraiva tapasi sthitaḥ .. 58 ..
5.65.d:
ततः शूद्रः स विज्ञाय तत्क्षेत्रं पुण्यवर्ध नम् ..
न जगाम गृहं भूयस्तत्रैव तपसि स्थितः .. 58 ..
5.65.m: Then that śūdra, knowing that sacred field to be an increaser of merit, / did not return home again, but remained right there engaged in austerity.

5.65.s:
gaṃgāyamunayoḥ pārśve śūdrakeśvarasaṃjñitam ..
ligaṃ saṃsthāpitaṃ tena sarvapātakanāśanam .. 59 ..
5.65.d:
गंगायमुनयोः पार्श्वे शूद्रकेश्वरसंज्ञितम् ..
लिगं संस्थापितं तेन सर्वपातकनाशनम् .. 59 ..
5.65.m: Beside the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, he installed a liṅga / named Śūdrakeśvara, which destroys all sins.

5.65.s:
yastayorvidhivatsnānaṃ kṛtvā pūjayate naraḥ ..
śūdrakeśvarasaṃjñaṃ ca liṃgaṃ śraddhāsamanvitaḥ .. 6.65.60 ..
5.65.d:
यस्तयोर्विधिवत्स्नानं कृत्वा पूजयते नरः ..
शूद्रकेश्वरसंज्ञं च लिंगं श्रद्धासमन्वितः .. 6.65.60 ..
5.65.m: Whatever man, having performed ritual ablution in both of them according to rule, worships / with faith the liṅga named Śūdrakeśvara,

5.65.s:
sa sarvaiḥ pātakairmuktaḥ prayāti śiva maṃdiram..
stūyamānaśca gaṃdharvairvimānavaramāśritaḥ .. 61 ..
5.65.d:
स सर्वैः पातकैर्मुक्तः प्रयाति शिव मंदिरम्..
स्तूयमानश्च गंधर्वैर्विमानवरमाश्रितः .. 61 ..
5.65.m: freed from all sins, he goes to the abode of Śiva, / praised by gandharvas and mounted on an excellent aerial chariot.

5.65.s:
yastatra tyajati prāṇānkṛtvā prāyopaveśanam ..
na ca bhūyo'tra saṃsāre sa janmāpnoti . mānavaḥ .. 62 ..
5.65.d:
यस्तत्र त्यजति प्राणान्कृत्वा प्रायोपवेशनम् ..
न च भूयोऽत्र संसारे स जन्माप्नोति . मानवः .. 62 ..
5.65.m: A man who gives up his life's breaths there by sitting down to fast unto death / is not born again in this cycle of worldly existence.

5.65.s:
gaṃḍūṣamapi toyasya yastasya nivasanpibet ..
so'pi saṃmucyate pāpādājanmamaraṇāṃtikāt..63..
5.65.d:
गंडूषमपि तोयस्य यस्तस्य निवसन्पिबेत् ..
सोऽपि संमुच्यते पापादाजन्ममरणांतिकात्..63..
5.65.m: He who, dwelling there, drinks even a mouthful of its water, / he too is liberated from sin accumulated from birth to death.

5.65.s:
yastatra brāhmaṇeṃdrāṇāṃ saṃprayacchati bhojanam ..
pitarastasya tṛpyaṃti yāvatkalpaśatatrayam .. 64 ..
5.65.d:
यस्तत्र ब्राह्मणेंद्राणां संप्रयच्छति भोजनम् ..
पितरस्तस्य तृप्यंति यावत्कल्पशतत्रयम् .. 64 ..
5.65.m: Whoever provides a meal there to the best of brahmins, / his ancestors remain satisfied for three hundred kalpas.

5.65.s:
truṭimātraṃ ca yo dadyāttatra svarṇaṃ samāhitaḥ ..
sa prāpnoti phalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ rājasūyāśvamedhayoḥ .. 65 ..
5.65.d:
त्रुटिमात्रं च यो दद्यात्तत्र स्वर्णं समाहितः ..
स प्राप्नोति फलं कृत्स्नं राजसूयाश्वमेधयोः .. 65 ..
5.65.m: And he who, composed in mind, gives even a particle of gold there, / obtains the entire fruit of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices.

5.65.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena tattīrthavaramāśrayet ..
ya icchecchāśvataṃ svargaṃ sadaiva manujo dvijāḥ .. 66 ..
5.65.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन तत्तीर्थवरमाश्रयेत् ..
य इच्छेच्छाश्वतं स्वर्गं सदैव मनुजो द्विजाः .. 66 ..
5.65.m: Therefore, with every effort, a man should resort to that excellent sacred ford, / if he ever desires eternal heaven, O twice-born!

5.65.s:
atra gāthā purā gītā gautamena maharṣiṇā..
gaṃgāyamunayostaṃ ca prabhāvaṃ vīkṣya vismayāt .. 67 ..
5.65.d:
अत्र गाथा पुरा गीता गौतमेन महर्षिणा..
गंगायमुनयोस्तं च प्रभावं वीक्ष्य विस्मयात् .. 67 ..
5.65.m: In this regard, a verse was sung in ancient times by the great seer Gautama, / seeing in amazement that power of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā:

5.65.s:
gaṃgāyamunayoḥ saṃge naraḥ snātvā samāhitaḥ ..
śūdreśvaraṃ samālokya sadyaḥ svargamavāpnuyāt .. 68 ..
5.65.d:
गंगायमुनयोः संगे नरः स्नात्वा समाहितः ..
शूद्रेश्वरं समालोक्य सद्यः स्वर्गमवाप्नुयात् .. 68 ..
5.65.m: "A man who, collected in mind, bathes at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā / and beholds Śūdreśvara, immediately attains heaven."

5.65.s:
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ gaṃgāyamunayormayā ..
māhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvapātakanāśanam .. 69 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe śrīhāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmya ānartakeśvaraśūdrakeśvaramāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma paṃcaṣaṣṭitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 65 .. ..
5.65.d:
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं गंगायमुनयोर्मया ..
माहात्म्यं ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठाः सर्वपातकनाशनम् .. 69 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे श्रीहाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्य आनर्तकेश्वरशूद्रकेश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम पंचषष्टितमोऽध्यायः .. 65 .. ..
5.65.m:
This whole māhātmya of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, / destroying all sins, has been told to you by me, O best of brahmins.
Thus ends the sixty-fifth chapter, named 'Description of the Māhātmya of Ānartakeśvara and Śūdrakeśvara', in the Māhātmya of the Sacred Field of Holy Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the sixth part of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.66.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tathā tatrāsti vikhyātaṃ rāmahrada iti smṛtam ..
yatra te pitarastena rudhireṇa pratarpitāḥ .. 1 ..
5.66.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तथा तत्रास्ति विख्यातं रामह्रद इति स्मृतम् ..
यत्र ते पितरस्तेन रुधिरेण प्रतर्पिताः .. 1 ..
5.66.m: Sūta said: / Likewise, there is a renowned [tīrtha] there, remembered as Rāmahrada, / where his ancestors were propitiated by him with blood.

5.66.s:
tatra bhādrapade māsi yo'māvāsyāmavāpya ca ..
pitṝnsaṃtarpayedbhaktyā so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet .. 2 ..
5.66.d:
तत्र भाद्रपदे मासि योऽमावास्यामवाप्य च ..
पितॄन्संतर्पयेद्भक्त्या सोऽश्वमेधफलं लभेत् .. 2 ..
5.66.m: Whoever, having arrived on the new moon day in the month of Bhādrapada, / propitiates the ancestors with devotion there, obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

5.66.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
atyāścaryamidaṃ sūta yadbravīṣi mahāmate ..
yattena pitarastatra rudhireṇa pratarpitāḥ .. 3 ..
5.66.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
अत्याश्चर्यमिदं सूत यद्ब्रवीषि महामते ..
यत्तेन पितरस्तत्र रुधिरेण प्रतर्पिताः .. 3 ..
5.66.m: The seers said: / This is a great wonder that you speak of, O wise one, / that his ancestors were propitiated there by him with blood!

5.66.s:
pitṛṇāṃ tarpaṇārthāya medhyāḥ saṃkīrtitā budhaiḥ ..
padārthā rudhiraṃ proktaṃ rākṣasānāṃ pratarpaṇe .. 4 ..
5.66.d:
पितृणां तर्पणार्थाय मेध्याः संकीर्तिता बुधैः ..
पदार्था रुधिरं प्रोक्तं राक्षसानां प्रतर्पणे .. 4 ..
5.66.m: Pure substances have been declared by the wise for the purpose of propitiating ancestors; / blood is prescribed for the propitiation of demons.

5.66.s:
śrutismṛtiviruddhaṃ ca karma sadbhirvigarhitam ..
jāmadagnyena taccīrṇaṃ kasmātsūta vadasva naḥ .. 5 ..
5.66.d:
श्रुतिस्मृतिविरुद्धं च कर्म सद्भिर्विगर्हितम् ..
जामदग्न्येन तच्चीर्णं कस्मात्सूत वदस्व नः .. 5 ..
5.66.m: And an act contrary to Śruti and Smṛti is condemned by the virtuous. / Why was that done by Jāmadagnya? Tell us, O Sūta!

5.66.s:
.. sūta uvāca.. ..
tena kopavaśātkarma pratijñāṃ parirakṣatā ..
tatkṛtaṃ tarpitā yena pitaro rudhireṇa te .. 6 ..
5.66.d:
.. सूत उवाच.. ..
तेन कोपवशात्कर्म प्रतिज्ञां परिरक्षता ..
तत्कृतं तर्पिता येन पितरो रुधिरेण ते .. 6 ..
5.66.m: Sūta said: / Under the influence of anger, while keeping his vow, / that deed was done by him, by which those ancestors were propitiated with blood.

5.66.s:
pitā tasya purā viprā jamadagnirnipātitaḥ ..
kṣatriyeṇa svadharmastho vinā doṣaṃ dvijottamāḥ .. 7 ..
5.66.d:
पिता तस्य पुरा विप्रा जमदग्निर्निपातितः ..
क्षत्रियेण स्वधर्मस्थो विना दोषं द्विजोत्तमाः .. 7 ..
5.66.m: In ancient times, O brahmins, his father Jamadagni, abiding in his own duty, / was struck down without fault by a kṣatriya, O best of the twice-born.

5.66.s:
tataḥ kopaparītena tena proktaṃ mahātmanā ..
raktena kṣatriyotthena saṃtarpyāḥ pitaro mayā .. 8 ..
5.66.d:
ततः कोपपरीतेन तेन प्रोक्तं महात्मना ..
रक्तेन क्षत्रियोत्थेन संतर्प्याः पितरो मया .. 8 ..
5.66.m: Then, overcome with anger, that noble one declared: / 'The ancestors shall be propitiated by me with blood arising from kṣatriyas!'

5.66.s:
etasmātkāraṇāttena rudhireṇa mahātmanā ..
pitarastarpitā samyaktilamiśreṇa bhaktitaḥ .. 9 ..
5.66.d:
एतस्मात्कारणात्तेन रुधिरेण महात्मना ..
पितरस्तर्पिता सम्यक्तिलमिश्रेण भक्तितः .. 9 ..
5.66.m: For this reason, the ancestors were duly propitiated by that noble one / with devotion, using blood mixed with sesame seeds.

5.66.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
jamadagnirhataḥ kasmātkṣatriyeṇa mahāmuniḥ ..
kiṃnāmā sa ca bhūpālo vistarādvada sūta tat .. 6.66.10 ..
5.66.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
जमदग्निर्हतः कस्मात्क्षत्रियेण महामुनिः ..
किंनामा स च भूपालो विस्तराद्वद सूत तत् .. 6.66.10 ..
5.66.m: The seers said: / Why was the great sage Jamadagni killed by the kṣatriya? / And what was the name of that king? Tell that in detail, O Sūta.

5.66.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
ṛcīkatanayaḥ pūrvaṃ jamadagniriti smṛtaḥ ..
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre tatrāsīddagdhakalmaṣaḥ .. 11 ..
5.66.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
ऋचीकतनयः पूर्वं जमदग्निरिति स्मृतः ..
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे तत्रासीद्दग्धकल्मषः .. 11 ..
5.66.m: Sūta said: / Formerly, the son of Ṛcīka, remembered as Jamadagni, / whose sins had been burned away, lived there in the sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara.

5.66.s:
catvārastasya putrāśca babhūvurguṇasaṃyutāḥ ..
jaghanyo'pi guṇajyeṣṭhasteṣāṃ rāmo babhūva ha .. 12 ..
5.66.d:
चत्वारस्तस्य पुत्राश्च बभूवुर्गुणसंयुताः ..
जघन्योऽपि गुणज्येष्ठस्तेषां रामो बभूव ह .. 12 ..
5.66.m: And he had four sons endowed with good qualities; / though the youngest, Rāma was indeed the eldest among them in virtue.

5.66.s:
kadācidvasatastasya jamadagnermahāvane ..
putreṣu kandamūlārthaṃ nirgateṣu vanādbahiḥ .. 13 ..
5.66.d:
कदाचिद्वसतस्तस्य जमदग्नेर्महावने ..
पुत्रेषु कन्दमूलार्थं निर्गतेषु वनाद्बहिः .. 13 ..
5.66.m: Once, while that Jamadagni was residing in the great forest, / and his sons had gone outside the forest for the sake of roots and tubers,

5.66.s:
etasminnaṃtare prāpto haihayādhipatirbalī ..
sahasrārjuna ityeva vikhyāto yo mahītale .. 14 ..
5.66.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राप्तो हैहयाधिपतिर्बली ..
सहस्रार्जुन इत्येव विख्यातो यो महीतले .. 14 ..
5.66.m: in the meantime, the mighty ruler of the Haihayas arrived, / he who was renowned on earth as Sahasrārjuna.

5.66.s:
mṛgalipsurvane tasminbhramamāṇa itastataḥ ..
śramārto vṛṣarāśisthe bhāskare dinamadhyage .. 15 ..
tatastamāśramaṃ dṛṣṭvā nānādruma samākulam ..
caturaṃgena sainyena sahitaḥ praviveśa ha ...6..
athāpaśyatsa tatrasthaṃ jamadagniṃ mahāmunim ..
upaviṣṭaṃ kṛtasnānaṃ devārcanaparāyaṇam...7..
5.66.d:
मृगलिप्सुर्वने तस्मिन्भ्रममाण इतस्ततः ..
श्रमार्तो वृषराशिस्थे भास्करे दिनमध्यगे .. 15 ..
ततस्तमाश्रमं दृष्ट्वा नानाद्रुम समाकुलम् ..
चतुरंगेन सैन्येन सहितः प्रविवेश ह ...6..
अथापश्यत्स तत्रस्थं जमदग्निं महामुनिम् ..
उपविष्टं कृतस्नानं देवार्चनपरायणम्...7..
5.66.m:
Desiring game, wandering here and there in that forest, / he was overcome with fatigue at midday when the sun stood in the sign of Taurus.
Then, seeing that hermitage crowded with diverse trees, / he entered it along with his fourfold army.
Then he saw the great sage Jamadagni staying there, / seated, having bathed, devoted to the worship of the gods.

5.66.s:
atha taṃ pārthivaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa munistuṣṭisaṃyutaḥ ..
arghaṃ dattvā yathānyāyaṃ svāgatenābhinaṃdya ca .. 18 ..
5.66.d:
अथ तं पार्थिवं दृष्ट्वा स मुनिस्तुष्टिसंयुतः ..
अर्घं दत्त्वा यथान्यायं स्वागतेनाभिनंद्य च .. 18 ..
5.66.m: Then, seeing that king, the sage was filled with pleasure; / having offered the respectful water offering according to rule and greeted him with welcome,

5.66.s:
so'pi taṃ praṇipatyoccairvinayena samanvitaḥ ..
pratisaṃbhāṣayāmāsa kuśalaṃ paryapṛcchata .. 19 ..
5.66.d:
सोऽपि तं प्रणिपत्योच्चैर्विनयेन समन्वितः ..
प्रतिसंभाषयामास कुशलं पर्यपृच्छत .. 19 ..
5.66.m: the king too, bowing deeply to him and filled with humility, / replied to him and inquired after his well-being.

5.66.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
kaccitte kuśalaṃ vipra putraśiṣyānvitasya ca ..
sāgnihotra kalatrasya parivārayutasya ca .. 6.66.20 ..
5.66.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
कच्चित्ते कुशलं विप्र पुत्रशिष्यान्वितस्य च ..
साग्निहोत्र कलत्रस्य परिवारयुतस्य च .. 6.66.20 ..
5.66.m: The king said: / "Is all well with you, O brahmin, and with your sons and disciples, / with your Agnihotra fires, your wife, and your retinue?

5.66.s:
adya me saphalaṃ janma jīvitaṃ saphalaṃ ca me ..
yattvaṃ taponidhirdṛṣṭaḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ .. 21 ..
5.66.d:
अद्य मे सफलं जन्म जीवितं सफलं च मे ..
यत्त्वं तपोनिधिर्दृष्टः सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः .. 21 ..
5.66.m: Today my birth is fruitful, and my life is fruitful, / since I have seen you, a treasure of austerity, revered by all the worlds."

5.66.s:
evamuktvā sa rājarṣirviśramya suciraṃ tataḥ ..
pītvāpastamuvācedaṃ praṇipatya mahāmunim.. 22 ..
5.66.d:
एवमुक्त्वा स राजर्षिर्विश्रम्य सुचिरं ततः ..
पीत्वापस्तमुवाचेदं प्रणिपत्य महामुनिम्.. 22 ..
5.66.m: Having spoken thus, that royal sage rested for a long time; / then, having drunk water and bowed down to that great sage, he said this:

5.66.s:
anujñāṃ dehi me brahmanprayāsyāmi nijaṃ gṛham..
mama kṛtyaṃ samādeśyaṃ yena te syātprayojanam .. 23 ..
5.66.d:
अनुज्ञां देहि मे ब्रह्मन्प्रयास्यामि निजं गृहम्..
मम कृत्यं समादेश्यं येन ते स्यात्प्रयोजनम् .. 23 ..
5.66.m: "Grant me permission, O brahmin; I shall depart for my own home. / Command some task of mine by which I may be of service to you."

5.66.s:
.. jamadagniruvāca .. ..
devatārcanavelāyāṃ tvaṃ me gṛhamupāgataḥ ..
manoratha iva dhyātaḥ sarvadevamayo'tithiḥ .. 24 ..
5.66.d:
.. जमदग्निरुवाच .. ..
देवतार्चनवेलायां त्वं मे गृहमुपागतः ..
मनोरथ इव ध्यातः सर्वदेवमयोऽतिथिः .. 24 ..
5.66.m: Jamadagni said: / "You have come to my home at the time of worshipping the gods, / like a cherished wish meditated upon—a guest embodying all the gods.

5.66.s:
tasmānme'sti parā prītirbhaktiśca nṛpasattama ..
tatkuruṣva mayā dattaṃ svahastenaiva bhojanam .. 25 ..
5.66.d:
तस्मान्मेऽस्ति परा प्रीतिर्भक्तिश्च नृपसत्तम ..
तत्कुरुष्व मया दत्तं स्वहस्तेनैव भोजनम् .. 25 ..
5.66.m: Therefore I have supreme pleasure and devotion, O best of kings; / accept, then, the meal offered by me with my own hand. // 25

5.66.s:
rājā vā brāhmaṇo vātha śūdro vāpyaṃtyajo'pi vā ..
vaiśvadevāntasaṃprāptaḥ so'tithiḥ svargasaṃkramaḥ .. 26 ..
5.66.d:
राजा वा ब्राह्मणो वाथ शूद्रो वाप्यंत्यजोऽपि वा ..
वैश्वदेवान्तसंप्राप्तः सोऽतिथिः स्वर्गसंक्रमः .. 26 ..
5.66.m: Whether king or brahmin, śūdra or even an outcaste, / he who arrives at the conclusion of the Vaiśvadeva rite is a guest, a bridge to heaven. // 26

5.66.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
mamaite sainikā brahmañchataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ..
tairabhuktaiḥ kathaṃ bhoktuṃ yujyate mama kīrtaya .. 27 ..
5.66.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
ममैते सैनिका ब्रह्मञ्छतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ..
तैरभुक्तैः कथं भोक्तुं युज्यते मम कीर्तय .. 27 ..
5.66.m: The king said: / These soldiers of mine, O brahmin, are in hundreds and thousands; / while they have not eaten, how is it fitting for me to eat? Tell me. // 27

5.66.s:
.. jamadagniruvāca .. ..
sarveṣāṃ sainikānāṃ te saṃpradāsyāmi bhojanam ..
nātra ciṃtā tvayā kāryā munirniṣkiṃcano hyaham .. 28 ..
5.66.d:
.. जमदग्निरुवाच .. ..
सर्वेषां सैनिकानां ते संप्रदास्यामि भोजनम् ..
नात्र चिंता त्वया कार्या मुनिर्निष्किंचनो ह्यहम् .. 28 ..
5.66.m: Jamadagni said: / I will provide food for all your soldiers; / you need have no worry about this, for I am a sage devoid of worldly possessions. // 28

5.66.s:
yaiṣā paśyati rājeṃdra dhenurbaddhā mamāṃtike ..
eṣā sūte manobhīṣṭaṃ prārthitā sarvadaiva hi .. 29 . ..
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tataśca kautukāviṣṭaḥ sa nṛpo dvijasattamāḥ ..
bāḍhamityeva saṃprocya tasminnevāśrame sthitaḥ .. 6.66.30 ..
5.66.d:
यैषा पश्यति राजेंद्र धेनुर्बद्धा ममांतिके ..
एषा सूते मनोभीष्टं प्रार्थिता सर्वदैव हि .. 29 . ..
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
ततश्च कौतुकाविष्टः स नृपो द्विजसत्तमाः ..
बाढमित्येव संप्रोच्य तस्मिन्नेवाश्रमे स्थितः .. 6.66.30 ..
5.66.m: This cow you see tied near me, O king of kings, / yields whatever the heart desires whenever asked. // 29 // / Sūta said: / Then, filled with wonder, that king, O best of brahmins, / said, “So be it,” and remained in that very hermitage. // 6.66.30

5.66.s:
tataḥ saṃtarpya devāṃśca pitṝṃśca tadanaṃtaram ..
pūjayitvā havirvāhaṃ brāhmaṇāṃśca tataḥ param .. 31 ..
5.66.d:
ततः संतर्प्य देवांश्च पितॄंश्च तदनंतरम् ..
पूजयित्वा हविर्वाहं ब्राह्मणांश्च ततः परम् .. 31 ..
5.66.m: Then, having gratified the gods and the ancestors thereafter, / and having honoured the fire and then the brahmins, // 31

5.66.s:
upaviṣṭastataḥ sārdhaṃ sarvairbhṛtyairbubhukṣitaiḥ ..
śramārtairvismayāviṣṭaiḥ kṛte tasya dvijottamāḥ .. 32 ..
5.66.d:
उपविष्टस्ततः सार्धं सर्वैर्भृत्यैर्बुभुक्षितैः ..
श्रमार्तैर्विस्मयाविष्टैः कृते तस्य द्विजोत्तमाः .. 32 ..
5.66.m: he then sat down together with all his hungry attendants, / who were afflicted by fatigue and filled with astonishment, after he had done that, O best of brahmins. // 32

5.66.s:
tataḥ sa prārthayāmāsa tāṃ dhenuṃ munisattamaḥ ..
yo yatprārthayate dehi bhojyārthaṃ tasya tacchubhe .. 33 ..
5.66.d:
ततः स प्रार्थयामास तां धेनुं मुनिसत्तमः ..
यो यत्प्रार्थयते देहि भोज्यार्थं तस्य तच्छुभे .. 33 ..
5.66.m: Then that best of sages addressed that cow: / “Whatever anyone requests to eat, give that to him, O auspicious one!” // 33

5.66.s:
tataḥ sā suṣuve dhenurannamuccāvacaṃ śubham ..
pakvānnaṃ ca viśeṣeṇa cittāhlādakaraṃ param .. 34 ..
5.66.d:
ततः सा सुषुवे धेनुरन्नमुच्चावचं शुभम् ..
पक्वान्नं च विशेषेण चित्ताह्लादकरं परम् .. 34 ..
5.66.m: Then that cow yielded varied, auspicious food, / especially cooked food bringing supreme delight to the heart. // 34

5.66.s:
tataḥ khādyaṃ ca cavyaṃ ca lehyaṃ coṣyaṃ tathaiva ca ..
vyaṃjanāni vicitrāṇi kaṣāyakaṭukāni ca ..
amlāni madhurāṇyeva tiktāni guṇavaṃti ca .. 35 ..
5.66.d:
ततः खाद्यं च चव्यं च लेह्यं चोष्यं तथैव च ..
व्यंजनानि विचित्राणि कषायकटुकानि च ..
अम्लानि मधुराण्येव तिक्तानि गुणवंति च .. 35 ..
5.66.m: Then [she yielded] food to be chewed, swallowed, licked, and sucked, / and diverse side-dishes—astringent and pungent, / sour, sweet, bitter, and wholesome. // 35

5.66.s:
evaṃ prāpya parāṃ tṛptiṃ tayā dhenvā sa bhūpatiḥ ..
sevakaiḥ sabalaiḥ sārdha mannairamṛtasaṃbhavaiḥ .. 36 ..
5.66.d:
एवं प्राप्य परां तृप्तिं तया धेन्वा स भूपतिः ..
सेवकैः सबलैः सार्ध मन्नैरमृतसंभवैः .. 36 ..
5.66.m: Having thus attained supreme satisfaction from that cow, that king, / together with his servants and army, with foods born of nectar, // 36

5.66.s:
tato bhuktyavasāne tu prārthayāmāsa bhūpatiḥ ..
tāṃ dhenuṃ vismayāviṣṭo jamadagniṃ mahāmunim .. 37 ..
5.66.d:
ततो भुक्त्यवसाने तु प्रार्थयामास भूपतिः ..
तां धेनुं विस्मयाविष्टो जमदग्निं महामुनिम् .. 37 ..
5.66.m: then, at the conclusion of the meal, filled with astonishment, / the king requested that cow from the great sage Jamadagni: // 37

5.66.s:
kāmadhenuriyaṃ brahmannārhāraṇyanivāsinām ..
munīnāṃ śāntacittānāṃ tasmādyaccha mama svayam .. 38 ..
5.66.d:
कामधेनुरियं ब्रह्मन्नार्हारण्यनिवासिनाम् ..
मुनीनां शान्तचित्तानां तस्माद्यच्छ मम स्वयम् .. 38 ..
5.66.m: “This wish-granting cow, O brahmin, is not fitting for forest dwellers, / sages of peaceful minds; therefore, give her to me yourself! // 38

5.66.s:
yenā'karānkaromyadya lokāṃstasyāḥ prabhāvataḥ ..
sādhayāmi ca durgasthāñchatrūnbhūribalānvitān .. 39 ..
5.66.d:
येनाऽकरान्करोम्यद्य लोकांस्तस्याः प्रभावतः ..
साधयामि च दुर्गस्थाञ्छत्रून्भूरिबलान्वितान् .. 39 ..
5.66.m: By her power, I will today make the people tax-free, / and conquer enemies entrenched in strongholds endowed with great strength. // 39

5.66.s:
evaṃ kṛte tava śreyo bhaviṣyati ca sadyaśaḥ ..
iha loke pare caiva tasmātkuru mayoditam .. 6.66.40 .. ..
5.66.d:
एवं कृते तव श्रेयो भविष्यति च सद्यशः ..
इह लोके परे चैव तस्मात्कुरु मयोदितम् .. 6.66.40 .. ..
5.66.m: When this is done, there will be your highest good and true renown / in this world and in the next; therefore, do what I have said!” // 6.66.40

5.66.s:
.. jamadagniruvāca .. ..
homadhenuriyaṃ rājanmamaikā prāṇasaṃmatā ..
adeyā sarvadā pūjyā tasmānnārhasi yācitum .. 41 ..
.. rājovāca .1 ..
5.66.d:
.. जमदग्निरुवाच .. ..
होमधेनुरियं राजन्ममैका प्राणसंमता ..
अदेया सर्वदा पूज्या तस्मान्नार्हसि याचितुम् .. 41 ..
.. राजोवाच .1 ..
5.66.m:
Jamadagni said: / “This is my sacrificial cow, O king, dear to me as my very life; / she cannot be given, but must always be revered; therefore, you ought not to beg for her.” // 41
The king said:

5.66.s:
ahaṃ śatasahasraṃ te yacchāmyasyāḥ kṛte dvija ..
dhenūnāmaparaṃ vittaṃ yāvanmātraṃ pravāṃchasi .. 42 ..
5.66.d:
अहं शतसहस्रं ते यच्छाम्यस्याः कृते द्विज ..
धेनूनामपरं वित्तं यावन्मात्रं प्रवांछसि .. 42 ..
5.66.m: “I will give you a hundred thousand cows in exchange for her, O twice-born, / or any other wealth, as much as you desire.” // 42

5.66.s:
.. jamadagniruvāca .. ..
avikreyā mahārāja sāmānyāpi hi gauḥ smṛtā ..
kiṃ punarhomadhenuryā prabhāvairīdṛśairyutā .. 43 ..
5.66.d:
.. जमदग्निरुवाच .. ..
अविक्रेया महाराज सामान्यापि हि गौः स्मृता ..
किं पुनर्होमधेनुर्या प्रभावैरीदृशैर्युता .. 43 ..
5.66.m: Jamadagni said: / “Even an ordinary cow is declared not to be sold, O great king; / what then of a sacrificial cow endowed with such powers? // 43

5.66.s:
vimohādbrāhmaṇo yo gāṃ vikrīṇāti dhanecchayā ..
vikrīṇāti na sandehaḥ sa nijāṃ jananīmiha .. 44 ..
5.66.d:
विमोहाद्ब्राह्मणो यो गां विक्रीणाति धनेच्छया ..
विक्रीणाति न सन्देहः स निजां जननीमिह .. 44 ..
5.66.m: A brahmin who through delusion sells a cow out of desire for wealth, / sells his own mother in this world, without a doubt. // 44

5.66.s:
surāṃ pītvā dvijaṃ hatvā dvijānāṃ niṣkṛtiḥ smṛtā ..
dhenuvikrayakartṝṇāṃ prāyaścittaṃ na vidyate .. 45 ..
5.66.d:
सुरां पीत्वा द्विजं हत्वा द्विजानां निष्कृतिः स्मृता ..
धेनुविक्रयकर्तॄणां प्रायश्चित्तं न विद्यते .. 45 ..
5.66.m: Expiation is prescribed for brahmins who drink alcohol or kill a twice-born, / but no expiation exists for those who sell a cow.” // 45

5.66.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
yadi yacchasi no vipra sāmnā dhenumimāṃ mama ..
balādapi hariṣyāmi tasmātsāmnā pradīyatām .. 46 ..
5.66.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
यदि यच्छसि नो विप्र साम्ना धेनुमिमां मम ..
बलादपि हरिष्यामि तस्मात्साम्ना प्रदीयताम् .. 46 ..
5.66.m: The king said: / “If you do not give me this cow by peaceful means, O brahmin, / I will take her by force; therefore, let her be given peacefully!” // 46

5.66.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tacchrutvā kopasaṃyukto jamadagnirdvijottamāḥ ..
astramastramiti procya samuttasthau sabhātalāt .. 47 ..
5.66.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तच्छ्रुत्वा कोपसंयुक्तो जमदग्निर्द्विजोत्तमाः ..
अस्त्रमस्त्रमिति प्रोच्य समुत्तस्थौ सभातलात् .. 47 ..
5.66.m: Sūta said: / Hearing that, Jamadagni, filled with anger, O best of brahmins, / shouted, “A weapon, a weapon!” and rose from the floor of the assembly. // 47

5.66.s:
tataste sevakāstasya nṛpateścittavedinaḥ ..
aprāptaśastraṃ taṃ vipraṃ nijaghnurniśitāyudhaiḥ .. 48 ..
5.66.d:
ततस्ते सेवकास्तस्य नृपतेश्चित्तवेदिनः ..
अप्राप्तशस्त्रं तं विप्रं निजघ्नुर्निशितायुधैः .. 48 ..
5.66.m: Then those servants of the king, discerning his mind, / struck that brahmin with sharp weapons before he could reach a weapon. // 48

5.66.s:
tasyaivaṃ vadhyamānasya jamadagnermahātmanaḥ ..
reṇukākhyā priyā bhāryā papātopari duḥkhitā .. .. 49 ..
5.66.d:
तस्यैवं वध्यमानस्य जमदग्नेर्महात्मनः ..
रेणुकाख्या प्रिया भार्या पपातोपरि दुःखिता .. .. 49 ..
5.66.m: As the great-souled Jamadagni was thus being slain, / his beloved wife named Reṇukā fell over him in grief. // 49

5.66.s:
sā'pi nānāvidhaistīkṣṇaiḥ khaṇḍitā varavarṇinī ..
āyuḥśeṣatayā prāṇairna kathaṃcidviyojitā .. 6.66.50 ..
5.66.d:
साऽपि नानाविधैस्तीक्ष्णैः खण्डिता वरवर्णिनी ..
आयुःशेषतया प्राणैर्न कथंचिद्वियोजिता .. 6.66.50 ..
5.66.m: She too, a fair-complexioned woman, was slashed with various sharp [weapons], / but because her lifespan remained, her life-breaths were somehow not separated. // 6.66.50

5.66.s:
evaṃ hatvā sa viprendraṃ jamadagniṃ mahīpatiḥ ..
tāṃ dhenuṃ kālayāmāsa yatra māhiṣmatī purī .. 51 ..
5.66.d:
एवं हत्वा स विप्रेन्द्रं जमदग्निं महीपतिः ..
तां धेनुं कालयामास यत्र माहिष्मती पुरी .. 51 ..
5.66.m: Having thus slain Jamadagni, the chief of brahmins, the king / drove that cow away toward where the city of Māhiṣmatī lay. // 51

5.66.s:
atha sā kālyamānā ca dhenuḥ kopasamanvitā ..
jamadagniṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā rarambha karuṇaṃ muhuḥ .. 52 ..
5.66.d:
अथ सा काल्यमाना च धेनुः कोपसमन्विता ..
जमदग्निं हतं दृष्ट्वा ररम्भ करुणं मुहुः .. 52 ..
5.66.m: Then that cow, being driven away and filled with wrath, / seeing Jamadagni slain, lowed plaintively again and again. // 52

5.66.s:
tasyāḥ saṃrambhamāṇāyā vaktramārgeṇa nirgatāḥ ..
pulindā dāruṇā medāḥ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ .. 53 ..
5.66.d:
तस्याः संरम्भमाणाया वक्त्रमार्गेण निर्गताः ..
पुलिन्दा दारुणा मेदाः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः .. 53 ..
5.66.m: As she bellowed, there emerged from her mouth / fierce Pulindas and Medas by hundreds and thousands, // 53

5.66.s:
nānāśastradharāḥ sarve yamadūtā ivāparāḥ ..
procustāṃ sādaraṃ dhenumājñāṃ dehi drutaṃ hi naḥ .. 54 ..
sā'bravīddhanyatāmetaddhaihayādhipaterbalam ..
atha taiḥ kopasaṃyuktairdāruṇairmlecchajātibhiḥ ..
vināśayitumārabdhaṃ śitaiḥ śastrairnirargalam .. 55 .1
5.66.d:
नानाशस्त्रधराः सर्वे यमदूता इवापराः ..
प्रोचुस्तां सादरं धेनुमाज्ञां देहि द्रुतं हि नः .. 54 ..
साऽब्रवीद्धन्यतामेतद्धैहयाधिपतेर्बलम् ..
अथ तैः कोपसंयुक्तैर्दारुणैर्म्लेच्छजातिभिः ..
विनाशयितुमारब्धं शितैः शस्त्रैर्निरर्गलम् .. 55 .1
5.66.m:
all bearing diverse weapons, like other messengers of Yama. / They said respectfully to the cow, “Give us your command swiftly!” // 54
She said, “Let this army of the ruler of the Haihayas be destroyed!” / Then, filled with anger, those fierce barbarian tribes / began to destroy [them] unchecked with sharp weapons. // 55

5.66.s:
na kaścitpuruṣasteṣāṃ sammukho'pyabhavadraṇe ..
kiṃ punaḥ sahasā yoddhuṃ bhayena mahatānvitaḥ .. 56 ..
5.66.d:
न कश्चित्पुरुषस्तेषां सम्मुखोऽप्यभवद्रणे ..
किं पुनः सहसा योद्धुं भयेन महतान्वितः .. 56 ..
5.66.m: Not a single man could even face them in battle, / overcome as he was with great fear, much less fight suddenly. // 56

5.66.s:
atha bhagnaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā vadhyamānaṃ samaṃtataḥ ..
pulindairdāruṇākāraiḥ procustaṃ mantriṇo nṛpam .. 57 ..
5.66.d:
अथ भग्नं बलं दृष्ट्वा वध्यमानं समंततः ..
पुलिन्दैर्दारुणाकारैः प्रोचुस्तं मन्त्रिणो नृपम् .. 57 ..
5.66.m: Then, seeing the army broken and being slaughtered on all sides / by the Pulindas of terrible form, the ministers spoke to the king: // 57

5.66.s:
tejohāniḥ parā te'dya jātā brahmavadhādvibho ..
tasmāddhenuṃ parityajya gamyatāṃ nijamaṃdiram .. 58 ..
5.66.d:
तेजोहानिः परा तेऽद्य जाता ब्रह्मवधाद्विभो ..
तस्माद्धेनुं परित्यज्य गम्यतां निजमंदिरम् .. 58 ..
5.66.m: “A supreme loss of your lustre has occurred today from the slaying of a brahmin, O lord; / therefore, abandon the cow and go to your own palace, // 58

5.66.s:
yāvannāgacchate tasya rāmonāma suto balī ..
no cettena hato'traiva sabalo vadhameṣyasi .. 59 ..
5.66.d:
यावन्नागच्छते तस्य रामोनाम सुतो बली ..
नो चेत्तेन हतोऽत्रैव सबलो वधमेष्यसि .. 59 ..
5.66.m: before his mighty son named Rāma arrives; / otherwise, slain right here along with your army, you will meet your death! // 59

5.66.s:
naiṣā śakyā balānnetuṃ kāmadhenurmahodayā ..
śaktirūpā karotyevaṃ yā sṛṣṭiṃ svayameva hi .. 6.66.60 ..
5.66.d:
नैषा शक्या बलान्नेतुं कामधेनुर्महोदया ..
शक्तिरूपा करोत्येवं या सृष्टिं स्वयमेव हि .. 6.66.60 ..
5.66.m: This wish-granting cow of great majesty cannot be taken by force; / being of the nature of power, she herself brings forth [such a] creation!” // 6.66.60

5.66.s:
tataḥ sa pārthivo bhītasteṣāṃ vākyādviśeṣataḥ ..
jagāma hitvā tāṃ dhenuṃ svasthānaṃ hatasevakaḥ .. 61 ..
5.66.d:
ततः स पार्थिवो भीतस्तेषां वाक्याद्विशेषतः ..
जगाम हित्वा तां धेनुं स्वस्थानं हतसेवकः .. 61 ..
5.66.m: Then that king, frightened, especially by their words, / abandoned that cow and went to his own place, his servants slain. // 61

5.66.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye jamadagnivadhavarṇanaṃnāma ṣaṭṣaṣṭitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 66 .. .. cha ..
5.66.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये जमदग्निवधवर्णनंनाम षट्षष्टितमोऽध्यायः .. 66 .. .. छ ..
5.66.m: Thus ends the sixty-sixth chapter, named “The Description of the Slaying of Jamadagni,” in the Māhātmya of Hāṭakeśvara Kṣetra, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the eighty-one-thousand-verse compendium of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa. // 66

5.67.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
etasminnaṃtare prāpto rāmo bhrātṛbhiranvitaḥ ..
phalāni kandamūlāni gṛhītvā''śramasammukhaḥ .. 1 ..
5.67.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राप्तो रामो भ्रातृभिरन्वितः ..
फलानि कन्दमूलानि गृहीत्वा'ऽश्रमसम्मुखः .. 1 ..
5.67.m: Sūta said: / In the meantime, Rāma arrived, accompanied by his brothers, / holding fruits, roots, and tubers, facing toward the hermitage. // 1

5.67.s:
sa dṛṣṭvā svāśramaṃ dhvastaṃ pulindairbahuśo vṛtam ..
lakuṭāśmaprahāraistu tāṃ dhenuṃ jarjarīkṛtām .. 2 ..
5.67.d:
स दृष्ट्वा स्वाश्रमं ध्वस्तं पुलिन्दैर्बहुशो वृतम् ..
लकुटाश्मप्रहारैस्तु तां धेनुं जर्जरीकृताम् .. 2 ..
5.67.m: He saw his hermitage destroyed and thronged with many Pulindas, / and that cow battered by blows of clubs and stones. // 2

5.67.s:
papraccha kimidaṃ sarvaṃ vyākulatvamupāgatam ..
āśramāspadamābhīraiḥ pulindaiśca samāvṛtam .. 3 ..
5.67.d:
पप्रच्छ किमिदं सर्वं व्याकुलत्वमुपागतम् ..
आश्रमास्पदमाभीरैः पुलिन्दैश्च समावृतम् .. 3 ..
5.67.m: He asked: "What is this distress that has overtaken everything, / and the grounds of the hermitage surrounded by Ābhīras and Pulindas?

5.67.s:
kenaiṣā māmikā dhenuḥ prahārairjarjarīkṛtā ..
tāpasyastāpasāḥ sarve kasmādete rudanti ca .. 4 ..
5.67.d:
केनैषा मामिका धेनुः प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृता ..
तापस्यस्तापसाः सर्वे कस्मादेते रुदन्ति च .. 4 ..
5.67.m: "By whom has this cow of mine been battered with blows? / And why are all these female and male ascetics weeping?

5.67.s:
kva sa me'dya pitā vṛddho mātā ca sutavatsalā ..
na māmadya yathāpūrvaṃ snehāccāyāti sammukhī .. 5 ..
5.67.d:
क्व स मेऽद्य पिता वृद्धो माता च सुतवत्सला ..
न मामद्य यथापूर्वं स्नेहाच्चायाति सम्मुखी .. 5 ..
5.67.m: "Where is my old father today, and my mother who loves her son? / Why does she not come out to meet me with affection today as before?"

5.67.s:
atha tasya samācakhyurvṛttāṃtaṃ sarvatāpasāḥ ..
yathādṛṣṭaṃ suduḥkhārtā sahasrārjunaceṣṭitam .. 6 ..
5.67.d:
अथ तस्य समाचख्युर्वृत्तांतं सर्वतापसाः ..
यथादृष्टं सुदुःखार्ता सहस्रार्जुनचेष्टितम् .. 6 ..
5.67.m: Then all the ascetics, afflicted with deep sorrow, / related the event to him just as it was seen—the deed of Sahasrārjuna.

5.67.s:
tataste bhrātaraḥ sarve vajrapātopamaṃ vacaḥ ..
śrutvā dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ śastraiḥ khaṃḍitaṃ janakaṃ nijam .. 7 ..
5.67.d:
ततस्ते भ्रातरः सर्वे वज्रपातोपमं वचः ..
श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा च तं शस्त्रैः खंडितं जनकं निजम् .. 7 ..
5.67.m: Then all those brothers, hearing that word like a thunderbolt's strike / and seeing their own father cut to pieces with weapons,

5.67.s:
mātaraṃ kṣatasarvāṅgīṃ prāṇaśeṣāṃ vyathānvitām..
ruruduḥ śokasantaptā muktvā rāmaṃ mahābalam.. 8 ..
5.67.d:
मातरं क्षतसर्वाङ्गीं प्राणशेषां व्यथान्विताम्..
रुरुदुः शोकसन्तप्ता मुक्त्वा रामं महाबलम्.. 8 ..
5.67.m: and their mother, all her limbs wounded, with only her breath remaining, filled with pain, / wept, consumed by grief, except for the mighty Rāma.

5.67.s:
ruditvātha ciraṃ kālaṃ vipralapya muhurmuhuḥ ..
antyeṣṭiṃ cakrire tasya vedoktavidhinā tataḥ .. 9 ..
5.67.d:
रुदित्वाथ चिरं कालं विप्रलप्य मुहुर्मुहुः ..
अन्त्येष्टिं चक्रिरे तस्य वेदोक्तविधिना ततः .. 9 ..
5.67.m: Having wept for a long time and lamented again and again, / they then performed his funeral rites according to the rule declared in the Vedas.

5.67.s:
atha dāhāvasāne te kṛtvā gartāṃ yathocitām..
muktvā rāmaṃ dadustoyaṃ pituḥ putrāstilānvitam .. 6.67.10 ..
5.67.d:
अथ दाहावसाने ते कृत्वा गर्तां यथोचिताम्..
मुक्त्वा रामं ददुस्तोयं पितुः पुत्रास्तिलान्वितम् .. 6.67.10 ..
5.67.m: Then, at the conclusion of the cremation, having dug a pit as was customary, / the sons, except for Rāma, offered water mixed with sesame seeds to their father.

5.67.s:
athānyaistāpasaiḥ prokto rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ ..
na prayacchasi kasmāttvaṃ pretapitre jalāṃjalim.. 11 ..
5.67.d:
अथान्यैस्तापसैः प्रोक्तो रामः शस्त्रभृतां वरः ..
न प्रयच्छसि कस्मात्त्वं प्रेतपित्रे जलांजलिम्.. 11 ..
5.67.m: Then Rāma, the best of weapon-bearers, was addressed by other ascetics: / "Why do you not offer a handful of water to your deceased father?"

5.67.s:
athāsau bahudhā pro ktastāpasairjamadagnijaḥ ..
prahārāngaṇayanmātuḥ śitaśastravinirmitān.. 12 ..
5.67.d:
अथासौ बहुधा प्रो क्तस्तापसैर्जमदग्निजः ..
प्रहारान्गणयन्मातुः शितशस्त्रविनिर्मितान्.. 12 ..
5.67.m: Then, being spoken to in many ways by the ascetics, that son of Jamadagni, / counting the wounds made upon his mother by sharp weapons,

5.67.s:
tatastānabravīdrāmo viniḥśvasya munīśvarān ..
niṣedhastoyadānasya śrūyatāṃ yanmayā kṛtaḥ .. 13 ..
5.67.d:
ततस्तानब्रवीद्रामो विनिःश्वस्य मुनीश्वरान् ..
निषेधस्तोयदानस्य श्रूयतां यन्मया कृतः .. 13 ..
5.67.m: then sighed deeply and said to those lords of sages: / "Listen to the reason for the refusal to offer water that was made by me.

5.67.s:
aparādhaṃ vinā tātaḥ kṣatriyeṇa hatomama ..
ekaviṃśatiḥ prahārāṇāṃ māturaṃge sthitā mama .. 14 ..
5.67.d:
अपराधं विना तातः क्षत्रियेण हतोमम ..
एकविंशतिः प्रहाराणां मातुरंगे स्थिता मम .. 14 ..
5.67.m: "Without any fault, my father was slain by a kṣatriya; / twenty-one wounds remain on the body of my mother.

5.67.s:
tasmānniḥkṣatriyāmurvīṃ yadyahaṃ na karomi vai ..
prahārasaṃkhyayā viprāstanme syātsarvapātakam .. 15 ..
5.67.d:
तस्मान्निःक्षत्रियामुर्वीं यद्यहं न करोमि वै ..
प्रहारसंख्यया विप्रास्तन्मे स्यात्सर्वपातकम् .. 15 ..
5.67.m: "Therefore, O brahmins, if I do not make the earth devoid of kṣatriyas / according to the number of those blows, may all that sin be mine—

5.67.s:
pitṛmātṛvadhājjātaṃ yatkṛtaṃ tena pāpmanā ..
kṣatriyāpasadenātra tathānyadapi kutsitam .. 16 ..
5.67.d:
पितृमातृवधाज्जातं यत्कृतं तेन पाप्मना ..
क्षत्रियापसदेनात्र तथान्यदपि कुत्सितम् .. 16 ..
5.67.m: "the sin born from the murder of father and mother committed here by that wicked one, / that vilest of kṣatriyas, and whatever other vile act [there may be]!

5.67.s:
tatastasyaiva cānyeṣāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ durātmanām ..
rudhiraiḥ pūrayitvemāṃ gartāṃ pitṛjalocitām ..
tarpayiṣyāmi raktena pitaraṃ nāhamaṃbhasā .. 17 ..
5.67.d:
ततस्तस्यैव चान्येषां क्षत्रियाणां दुरात्मनाम् ..
रुधिरैः पूरयित्वेमां गर्तां पितृजलोचिताम् ..
तर्पयिष्यामि रक्तेन पितरं नाहमंभसा .. 17 ..
5.67.m: "Then, having filled this pit intended for the paternal water with the blood / of that very one and of other evil-minded kṣatriyas, / I will gratify my father with blood, not with water!"

5.67.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
śrutvā te dāruṇāṃ tasya pratijñāṃ tāpasottamāḥ ..
paraṃ vismayamāpannā nocuḥ kiṃcittataḥ param .. 19 ..
athāśaucāṃtamāsādya rāmaḥ krodhasamanvitaḥ ..
tīkṣṇaṃ paraśumādāya māhiṣmatyunmukhaṃ yayau .. 19 ..
5.67.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
श्रुत्वा ते दारुणां तस्य प्रतिज्ञां तापसोत्तमाः ..
परं विस्मयमापन्ना नोचुः किंचित्ततः परम् .. 19 ..
अथाशौचांतमासाद्य रामः क्रोधसमन्वितः ..
तीक्ष्णं परशुमादाय माहिष्मत्युन्मुखं ययौ .. 19 ..
5.67.m:
Sūta said: / Hearing his terrible vow, those best of ascetics / were filled with supreme astonishment and said nothing further.
Then, after the period of ritual impurity had ended, Rāma, filled with rage, / took his sharp axe and set out toward Māhiṣmatī,

5.67.s:
sarvaistaiḥ śabaraiḥ sārdhaṃ pulindairmedakaistathā ..
baddhagodhāṃgulitrāṇairvarabāṇadhanurdharaiḥ .. 6.67.20 ..
5.67.d:
सर्वैस्तैः शबरैः सार्धं पुलिन्दैर्मेदकैस्तथा ..
बद्धगोधांगुलित्राणैर्वरबाणधनुर्धरैः .. 6.67.20 ..
5.67.m: together with all those Śabaras, Pulindas, and Medakas, / wearing leather armguards and finger-guards, bearing excellent arrows and bows.

5.67.s:
tathā'rjuno'pi taṃ śrutvā samāyātaṃ bhṛgūttamam ..
sainyena mahatā yuktaṃ pratijñādhāriṇaṃ tathā .. 21 ..
5.67.d:
तथाऽर्जुनोऽपि तं श्रुत्वा समायातं भृगूत्तमम् ..
सैन्येन महता युक्तं प्रतिज्ञाधारिणं तथा .. 21 ..
5.67.m: Arjuna too, hearing that he, the best of the Bhṛgus, had arrived / accompanied by a great army and bound by a vow,

5.67.s:
tatastu sammukho dṛṣṭo yuddhārthaṃ sa viniryayau ..
sārdhaṃ nānāvidhairyodhaiḥ sarvairdevāsuropamaiḥ .. 22 ..
5.67.d:
ततस्तु सम्मुखो दृष्टो युद्धार्थं स विनिर्ययौ ..
सार्धं नानाविधैर्योधैः सर्वैर्देवासुरोपमैः .. 22 ..
5.67.m: then, having seen [him], went out to face [him] for battle / accompanied by various warriors, all resembling gods and asuras.

5.67.s:
athābhavanmahāyuddhaṃ pulindānāṃ dvijottamāḥ ..
haihayādhipateryodhaiḥ sārdhaṃ devāsuropamaiḥ .. 23 ..
5.67.d:
अथाभवन्महायुद्धं पुलिन्दानां द्विजोत्तमाः ..
हैहयाधिपतेर्योधैः सार्धं देवासुरोपमैः .. 23 ..
5.67.m: Then, O best of the twice-born, a great battle took place between the Pulindas / and the warriors of the lord of the Haihayas, who resembled gods and asuras.

5.67.s:
tataste haihayāḥ sarve śarairāśīviṣopamaiḥ ..
vadhyante śabaraiḥ saṃkhye garjamānairmuhurmuhuḥ .. 24 ..
5.67.d:
ततस्ते हैहयाः सर्वे शरैराशीविषोपमैः ..
वध्यन्ते शबरैः संख्ये गर्जमानैर्मुहुर्मुहुः .. 24 ..
5.67.m: Then all those Haihayas were slain in battle / by the Śabaras roaring repeatedly, with arrows resembling venomous serpents.

5.67.s:
brahmahatyāsamutthena pātakena tataśca te ..
jātā nistejasaḥ sarve prapataṃti dharātale .. 25 ..
5.67.d:
ब्रह्महत्यासमुत्थेन पातकेन ततश्च ते ..
जाता निस्तेजसः सर्वे प्रपतंति धरातले .. 25 ..
5.67.m: Then, by the sin arising from the murder of a brahmin, / all of them were deprived of their splendor and fell down upon the surface of the earth.

5.67.s:
na kaścitpauruṣaṃ tatra saṃpradarśayituṃ kṣamaḥ ..
palāyanaparā sarve vadhyante niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ .. 26 ..
5.67.d:
न कश्चित्पौरुषं तत्र संप्रदर्शयितुं क्षमः ..
पलायनपरा सर्वे वध्यन्ते निशितैः शरैः .. 26 ..
5.67.m: None there was able to display manly prowess; / all intent on flight, they were struck down by sharp arrows.

5.67.s:
atha bhagnaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā haihayādhipatiḥ krudhā ..
svacāpaṃ vāñchayāmāsa sajyaṃ kartuṃ tvarānvitaḥ ..
śaknoti nāropayituṃ suyatnamapi cāśritaḥ .. 27 ..
5.67.d:
अथ भग्नं बलं दृष्ट्वा हैहयाधिपतिः क्रुधा ..
स्वचापं वाञ्छयामास सज्यं कर्तुं त्वरान्वितः ..
शक्नोति नारोपयितुं सुयत्नमपि चाश्रितः .. 27 ..
5.67.m: Then, seeing his army broken, the lord of the Haihayas in rage / desired to string his bow in haste, / but though he made a great effort, he was unable to string it.

5.67.s:
tataścākarṣayāmāsa khaṅgaṃ kośātsunirmalam ..
ākraṣṭuṃ na ca śakroti vailakṣyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ .. 28 ..
5.67.d:
ततश्चाकर्षयामास खङ्गं कोशात्सुनिर्मलम् ..
आक्रष्टुं न च शक्रोति वैलक्ष्यं परमं गतः .. 28 ..
5.67.m: Then he drew his spotless sword from its scabbard, / but was unable to wield it, having fallen into supreme bewilderment.

5.67.s:
gadayā nirjito raudro rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ ..
yayā sāpyapataddhastāttatkṣaṇātpṛthivītale .. 29 ..
5.67.d:
गदया निर्जितो रौद्रो रावणो लोकरावणः ..
यया साप्यपतद्धस्तात्तत्क्षणात्पृथिवीतले .. 29 ..
5.67.m: The mace by which fierce Rāvaṇa, the terror of the world, was vanquished, / even that fell from his hand at that very instant onto the surface of the earth.

5.67.s:
narmadāyāḥ pravāho yaiḥ sahasrākhyaiḥ karaiḥ śubhaiḥ ..
vidhṛtastena te sarve babhūvuḥ kampavihvalāḥ .. 6.67.30 ..
5.67.d:
नर्मदायाः प्रवाहो यैः सहस्राख्यैः करैः शुभैः ..
विधृतस्तेन ते सर्वे बभूवुः कम्पविह्वलाः .. 6.67.30 ..
5.67.m: Those auspicious hands, called a thousand, by which the flow of the Narmadā / had been held back—all of them became overcome with trembling.

5.67.s:
na śastraṃ śekuruddhartuṃ daivayogātkathaṃcana ..
divyāstrāṇāṃ tathā sarve mantrā vismṛtimāgatāḥ .. 31 ..
5.67.d:
न शस्त्रं शेकुरुद्धर्तुं दैवयोगात्कथंचन ..
दिव्यास्त्राणां तथा सर्वे मन्त्रा विस्मृतिमागताः .. 31 ..
5.67.m: Due to the power of fate, they could not lift any weapon whatsoever, / and all the mantras of the celestial weapons passed into oblivion.

5.67.s:
etasminnaṃtare rāmaḥ saṃprāptaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ ..
tīkṣṇaṃ paraśumudyamya tatastaṃ prāha niṣṭhuram .. 32 ..
5.67.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे रामः संप्राप्तः क्रोधमूर्छितः ..
तीक्ष्णं परशुमुद्यम्य ततस्तं प्राह निष्ठुरम् .. 32 ..
5.67.m: In the meantime, Rāma arrived, stupified with fury; / raising his sharp axe, he then said harsh words to him:

5.67.s:
haihayādhipate pāpa yaiḥ karairjanako mama ..
tvayā vinihatastānme śīghraṃ darśaya sāṃpratam .. 33 ..
5.67.d:
हैहयाधिपते पाप यैः करैर्जनको मम ..
त्वया विनिहतस्तान्मे शीघ्रं दर्शय सांप्रतम् .. 33 ..
5.67.m: "O sinful lord of the Haihayas, those hands with which / my father was struck down by you—show them to me quickly now!"

5.67.s:
brahmatejohataḥ so'pi proktastena suniṣṭhuram ..
novāca cottaraṃ kiṃcidālekhye likhito yathā ..34..
5.67.d:
ब्रह्मतेजोहतः सोऽपि प्रोक्तस्तेन सुनिष्ठुरम् ..
नोवाच चोत्तरं किंचिदालेख्ये लिखितो यथा ..34..
5.67.m: Stricken by brahminical power, though spoken to so harshly by him, / he did not speak any reply, like a figure painted in a picture.

5.67.s:
tato bhujavanaṃ tasya rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ ..
muhurmuhurvinirbhartsya pracakarta śanaiḥśanaiḥ .. 35 ..
5.67.d:
ततो भुजवनं तस्य रामः शस्त्रभृतां वरः ..
मुहुर्मुहुर्विनिर्भर्त्स्य प्रचकर्त शनैःशनैः .. 35 ..
5.67.m: Then Rāma, the best of weapon-bearers, repeatedly rebuking him, / cut down the forest of his arms little by little.

5.67.s:
tataśchittvā śirastasya kuṭhāreṇa bhṛgūdvahaḥ ..
jagrāha rudhiraṃ yatnātprahārebhyaḥ svayaṃ dvijāḥ .. 36 ..
5.67.d:
ततश्छित्त्वा शिरस्तस्य कुठारेण भृगूद्वहः ..
जग्राह रुधिरं यत्नात्प्रहारेभ्यः स्वयं द्विजाः .. 36 ..
5.67.m: Then, having severed his head with the axe, that scion of Bhṛgu / himself carefully took the blood from the wounds, O twice-born.

5.67.s:
pūrayitvā mahākumbhāñchabarebhyo dadau tataḥ ..
mlecchebhyo lubdhakebhyaśca tataḥ provāca sādaram ..37..
5.67.d:
पूरयित्वा महाकुम्भाञ्छबरेभ्यो ददौ ततः ..
म्लेच्छेभ्यो लुब्धकेभ्यश्च ततः प्रोवाच सादरम् ..37..
5.67.m: Having filled large jars, he then gave them to the Śabaras, / Mlecchas, and hunters, and then respectfully said:

5.67.s:
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre gartā me bhrātṛbhiḥ kṛtā ..
pitṛsaṃtarpaṇārthāya salilena pariplutā .. 38 ..
5.67.d:
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे गर्ता मे भ्रातृभिः कृता ..
पितृसंतर्पणार्थाय सलिलेन परिप्लुता .. 38 ..
5.67.m: "In the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara, a pit has been dug by my brothers / for the sake of gratifying my father, [now] filled with water.

5.67.s:
prakṣipadhvaṃ drutaṃ gatvā tasyāṃ raktamidaṃ mahat ..
pāpasyāsya sapatnasya mamādeśādasaṃśayam .. 39 ..
5.67.d:
प्रक्षिपध्वं द्रुतं गत्वा तस्यां रक्तमिदं महत् ..
पापस्यास्य सपत्नस्य ममादेशादसंशयम् .. 39 ..
5.67.m: "Go quickly and pour this great blood into it— / the blood of this sinful enemy—by my command, beyond doubt;

5.67.s:
yena tātaṃ nijaṃ bhaktyā tarpayitvā vidhānataḥ ..
ṛṇasya muktirbhavati yena me paitṛkasyaca .. 6.67.40 ..
5.67.d:
येन तातं निजं भक्त्या तर्पयित्वा विधानतः ..
ऋणस्य मुक्तिर्भवति येन मे पैतृकस्यच .. 6.67.40 ..
5.67.m: "so that, having gratified my own father with devotion according to the rite, / there may be liberation for me from the paternal debt."

5.67.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśātisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye sahasrārjunavadhavarṇanaṃnāma saptaṣaṣṭitamo' dhyāyaḥ .. 67 .. .. dha ..
5.67.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशातिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये सहस्रार्जुनवधवर्णनंनाम सप्तषष्टितमो' ध्यायः .. 67 .. .. ध ..
5.67.m: Thus ends the sixty-seventh chapter, entitled "The Description of the Slaying of Sahasrārjuna," in the Māhātmya of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.68.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
atha te śabarā yatnādraktaṃ taddhaihayodbhavam ..
tatra ninyuḥ sthitā yatra gartā sā pitṛsaṃbhavā .. 1 ..
5.68.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अथ ते शबरा यत्नाद्रक्तं तद्धैहयोद्भवम् ..
तत्र निन्युः स्थिता यत्र गर्ता सा पितृसंभवा .. 1 ..
5.68.m: Sūta said: / Then those Śabaras carefully carried that blood born from the Haihaya / to where that pit dug for the father was situated.

5.68.s:
bhārgavo'pi ca taṃ hatvā raktamādāya kṛtsnaśaḥ ..
tataḥ saṃpreṣayāmāsa yatra gartā'tha paitṛkī .. 2 ..
5.68.d:
भार्गवोऽपि च तं हत्वा रक्तमादाय कृत्स्नशः ..
ततः संप्रेषयामास यत्र गर्ताऽथ पैतृकी .. 2 ..
5.68.m: And the descendant of Bhṛgu, having slain him and taken all the blood, / then dispatched it to where the paternal pit was.

5.68.s:
na sa bālaṃ na vṛddhaṃ ca parityajati bhārgavaḥ ..
yauvanasthaṃ viśeṣeṇa garbhasthaṃ vātha kṣatriyam .. 3 ..
5.68.d:
न स बालं न वृद्धं च परित्यजति भार्गवः ..
यौवनस्थं विशेषेण गर्भस्थं वाथ क्षत्रियम् .. 3 ..
5.68.m: That descendant of Bhṛgu spared neither child nor old man, / nor one in the prime of youth, nor even a kṣatriya still in the womb.

5.68.s:
svayaṃ jaghāna bhūpānsa teṣāṃ pārśve tathā parān ..
vidhvaṃsāyayati kruddhaḥ sainikaiśca samantataḥ .. 4 ..
5.68.d:
स्वयं जघान भूपान्स तेषां पार्श्वे तथा परान् ..
विध्वंसाययति क्रुद्धः सैनिकैश्च समन्ततः .. 4 ..
5.68.m: He personally slew the kings and others beside them, / and enraged, he caused them to be destroyed on all sides by his soldiers.

5.68.s:
tathaivāsṛkpragṛhṇāti gṛhṇāpayati cādarāt ..
teṣāṃ pārśvaistatastūrṇaṃ preṣayāmāsa tatra ca .. 5 ..
5.68.d:
तथैवासृक्प्रगृह्णाति गृह्णापयति चादरात् ..
तेषां पार्श्वैस्ततस्तूर्णं प्रेषयामास तत्र च .. 5 ..
5.68.m: In the same manner he collected their blood, carefully made others collect it, / and through those at his side quickly had it sent there.

5.68.s:
evaṃ niḥkṣatriyāṃ kṛtvā kṛtsnāṃ pṛthvīṃ bhṛgadvahaḥ ..
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre jagāma tadanantaram .. 6 ..
5.68.d:
एवं निःक्षत्रियां कृत्वा कृत्स्नां पृथ्वीं भृगद्वहः ..
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे जगाम तदनन्तरम् .. 6 ..
5.68.m: Having thus made the entire earth devoid of kṣatriyas, that scion of Bhṛgu / went immediately thereafter to the sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara.

5.68.s:
tatastai rudhiraiḥ snātvā samādāya tilānbahūn ..
apasavyaṃ samādhāya pracakre pitṛtarpaṇam .. 7 ..
5.68.d:
ततस्तै रुधिरैः स्नात्वा समादाय तिलान्बहून् ..
अपसव्यं समाधाय प्रचक्रे पितृतर्पणम् .. 7 ..
5.68.m: Then, having bathed in that blood and taken many sesame seeds, / placing [his sacred thread] over the right shoulder, he performed the tarpaṇa for the ancestors.

5.68.s:
pratyakṣaṃ sarvaviprāṇāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ tapasvinām ..
pratijñāṃ pūrayitvā'tha viśokaḥ sa babhūva ha .. 8 ..
5.68.d:
प्रत्यक्षं सर्वविप्राणां तथान्येषां तपस्विनाम् ..
प्रतिज्ञां पूरयित्वाऽथ विशोकः स बभूव ह .. 8 ..
5.68.m: Before the eyes of all the brahmins as well as the other ascetics, / having fulfilled his vow, he became free from grief.

5.68.s:
tato niḥkṣatriye loke kṛtvā hayamakhaṃ ca saḥ ..
prāyacchatsakalāmurvīṃ brāhmaṇebhyaśca dakṣiṇām .. 9 ..
5.68.d:
ततो निःक्षत्रिये लोके कृत्वा हयमखं च सः ..
प्रायच्छत्सकलामुर्वीं ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च दक्षिणाम् .. 9 ..
5.68.m: Then, when the world was cleared of kṣatriyas, he performed a horse sacrifice / and granted the entire earth to the brahmins as their sacrificial fee.

5.68.s:
atha labdhavarā viprāstamūcurbhṛgusattamam ..
nāsmadbhūmau tvayā stheyameko rājā yataḥ smṛtaḥ .. 6.68.10 ..
so'pi bāḍhamiti procya harṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ ..
mahīparyaṃtamāsādya provācātha nadīpatim ......
āropya sumahaccāpamāgneyāstraṃ prayujya ca ..
triśikhāṃ bhrukuṭīṃ kṛtvā kopena mahatānvitaḥ ...2..
.. rāma uvāca .. ..
mayā niḥkṣatriyā bhūmiḥ kṛtā śailavanānvitā ..
brāhmaṇebhyastato dattā vājimedhe mahāmakhe ...3..
5.68.d:
अथ लब्धवरा विप्रास्तमूचुर्भृगुसत्तमम् ..
नास्मद्भूमौ त्वया स्थेयमेको राजा यतः स्मृतः .. 6.68.10 ..
सोऽपि बाढमिति प्रोच्य हर्षेण महतान्वितः ..
महीपर्यंतमासाद्य प्रोवाचाथ नदीपतिम् ......
आरोप्य सुमहच्चापमाग्नेयास्त्रं प्रयुज्य च ..
त्रिशिखां भ्रुकुटीं कृत्वा कोपेन महतान्वितः ...2..
.. राम उवाच .. ..
मया निःक्षत्रिया भूमिः कृता शैलवनान्विता ..
ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्ततो दत्ता वाजिमेधे महामखे ...3..
5.68.m:
Then the brahmins, having obtained the boons, said to that best of the Bhṛgus: / 'You must not remain on our land, for a king is traditionally considered singular.'
Saying 'Very well,' he, filled with great joy, / approached the edge of the earth and spoke to the lord of rivers [the Ocean]. / Stringing his mighty bow and fitting the fire weapon, / he knitted his brows into three furrows, filled with great wrath.
Rāma said: / 'I have made the earth, with its mountains and forests, devoid of kṣatriyas / and then given it to the brahmins in the great horse sacrifice.

5.68.s:
tasmāttvaṃ dehi me sthānaṃ kṛtvā'pasaraṇaṃ svayam..
na hi dattvā grahī ṣyāmi viprebhyo medinīṃ punaḥ .. 14 ..
5.68.d:
तस्मात्त्वं देहि मे स्थानं कृत्वाऽपसरणं स्वयम्..
न हि दत्त्वा ग्रही ष्यामि विप्रेभ्यो मेदिनीं पुनः .. 14 ..
5.68.m: Therefore, make way yourself and give me a place. / For having given the earth to the brahmins, I will not take it back again.

5.68.s:
na karoṣyathavā vākyaṃ mamādya tvaṃ nadīpate ..
sthalarūpaṃ kariṣyāmi vahnyastrapariśoṣitam .. 15 ..
5.68.d:
न करोष्यथवा वाक्यं ममाद्य त्वं नदीपते ..
स्थलरूपं करिष्यामि वह्न्यस्त्रपरिशोषितम् .. 15 ..
5.68.m: If you do not obey my command today, O lord of rivers, / I will dry you up with the fire weapon and turn you into dry land.'

5.68.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā samudro bhayasaṃkulaḥ ..
apasāraṃ tataścakre yāvattasyābhivāṃchitam .. 16 ..
tataścakāra tatraiva vasatiṃ sa bhṛgūdvahaḥ ..
tapaścaryāsamāyuktaḥ piturvadhamanusmaran...7..
tataḥ sarvānpulindāṃśca śavarānmedasaṃyutān ..
bhūmyante dhārayāmāsa parvateṣu sa bhārgavaḥ ...8..
5.68.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा समुद्रो भयसंकुलः ..
अपसारं ततश्चक्रे यावत्तस्याभिवांछितम् .. 16 ..
ततश्चकार तत्रैव वसतिं स भृगूद्वहः ..
तपश्चर्यासमायुक्तः पितुर्वधमनुस्मरन्...7..
ततः सर्वान्पुलिन्दांश्च शवरान्मेदसंयुतान् ..
भूम्यन्ते धारयामास पर्वतेषु स भार्गवः ...8..
5.68.m:
Sūta said: / Hearing his words, the Ocean, agitated with fear, / thereupon withdrew as far as he desired.
Then that scion of Bhṛgu took up residence right there, / engaged in austerity and remembering the slaying of his father.
Then that descendant of Bhṛgu settled all the Pulindas / and the Śabaras together with the Medas at the edge of the land, on the mountains.

5.68.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye paraśurāmakṛtamahīdānapūrvakasamudrāpasāraṇavṛttāntavarṇanaṃnāmā ṣṭāṣaṣṭitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 68 .. .. cha ..
5.68.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये परशुरामकृतमहीदानपूर्वकसमुद्रापसारणवृत्तान्तवर्णनंनामा ष्टाषष्टितमोऽध्यायः .. 68 .. .. छ ..
5.68.m: Thus ends the sixty-eighth chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Ocean's Retreat Preceded by the Gift of the Earth by Paraśurāma', in the māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara sacred field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the auspicious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.69.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tato niḥkṣatriye loke kṣattriṇyo vaṃśakāraṇāt ..
kṣetrajānbrāhmaṇebhyaśca suṣuvustanayā nvarān.....
te vṛddhiṃ ca samāsādya kṣetrajāḥ kṣatriyopamāḥ ..
jagṛhurmedinīṃ vīryātsaṃnirasya dvijottamān..2..
5.69.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
ततो निःक्षत्रिये लोके क्षत्त्रिण्यो वंशकारणात् ..
क्षेत्रजान्ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च सुषुवुस्तनया न्वरान्.....
ते वृद्धिं च समासाद्य क्षेत्रजाः क्षत्रियोपमाः ..
जगृहुर्मेदिनीं वीर्यात्संनिरस्य द्विजोत्तमान्..2..
5.69.m: Sūta said: / Then, when the world was stripped of kṣatriyas, the kṣatriya women, for the sake of lineage, / gave birth through brahmins to excellent field-born sons. / These field-born sons, resembling kṣatriyas, grew to maturity, / and by their prowess expelled the best of the twice-born and seized the earth.

5.69.s:
tataste brāhmaṇāḥ sarve paribhūtipadaṃ gatāḥ..
procurbhārgavamabhyetya duḥkhena mahatānvitāḥ.. 3 ..
5.69.d:
ततस्ते ब्राह्मणाः सर्वे परिभूतिपदं गताः..
प्रोचुर्भार्गवमभ्येत्य दुःखेन महतान्विताः.. 3 ..
5.69.m: Then all those brahmins, having been brought to humilation, / approached the descendant of Bhṛgu and spoke, overcome with great distress:

5.69.s:
rāmarāma mahābāho yā tvayā vasudhā ca naḥ ..
vājimedhe makhe dattā kṣatriyaiḥ sā hatā balāt..
tasmānno dehi tāṃ bhūyo hatvā tānkṣatriyādhamān ..
kuru śreyo'bhivṛddhiṃ tāṃ yadyasti tava pauruṣam .. 5 ..
5.69.d:
रामराम महाबाहो या त्वया वसुधा च नः ..
वाजिमेधे मखे दत्ता क्षत्रियैः सा हता बलात्..
तस्मान्नो देहि तां भूयो हत्वा तान्क्षत्रियाधमान् ..
कुरु श्रेयोऽभिवृद्धिं तां यद्यस्ति तव पौरुषम् .. 5 ..
5.69.m: 'O Rāma, Rāma of mighty arms, the earth that was given by you to us / in the horse sacrifice has been seized by force by the kṣatriyas. / Therefore, slay those vile kṣatriyas and give it to us once more; / cause that increase of our welfare, if your manhood remains!'

5.69.s:
tato rāmaḥ krudhāviṣṭo bhūyastaiḥ śavaraiḥ saha ..
pulindairmedakaiścaiva kṣatriyāṃtāya niryayau .. 6 ..
5.69.d:
ततो रामः क्रुधाविष्टो भूयस्तैः शवरैः सह ..
पुलिन्दैर्मेदकैश्चैव क्षत्रियांताय निर्ययौ .. 6 ..
5.69.m: Then Rāma, seized with wrath, set out again with those Śabaras, / Pulindas, and Medakas to put an end to the kṣatriyas.

5.69.s:
tatraiva kṣatriyānhatvā raktamādāya tadbahu ..
tāṃ gartāṃ pūrayāmāsa cakāra pitṛtarpaṇam .. 7 ..
5.69.d:
तत्रैव क्षत्रियान्हत्वा रक्तमादाय तद्बहु ..
तां गर्तां पूरयामास चकार पितृतर्पणम् .. 7 ..
5.69.m: Slaying the kṣatriyas right there and taking their copious blood, / he filled that pit and performed the tarpaṇa for the ancestors.

5.69.s:
pradadau brāhmaṇebhyaśca vājimedhe dharāṃ punaḥ ..
taiśca nirvāsitastatra jagāmodadhisaṃnidhau .. 8 ..
5.69.d:
प्रददौ ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च वाजिमेधे धरां पुनः ..
तैश्च निर्वासितस्तत्र जगामोदधिसंनिधौ .. 8 ..
5.69.m: He gave the earth again to the brahmins in a horse sacrifice, / and banished by them there, he went to the proximity of the ocean.

5.69.s:
evaṃ tena kṛtā pṛthvī sarvakṣattravivarjitā ..
triḥsaptavāraṃ vipreṃdrā dvijebhyaśca niveditā .. 9 ..
5.69.d:
एवं तेन कृता पृथ्वी सर्वक्षत्त्रविवर्जिता ..
त्रिःसप्तवारं विप्रेंद्रा द्विजेभ्यश्च निवेदिता .. 9 ..
5.69.m: In this manner, the earth was cleared of all kṣatriyas by him / twenty-one times, O best of brahmins, and presented to the twice-born.

5.69.s:
tarpitāḥ pitaraścaiva rudhireṇa mahātmanā ..
pratijñā pālitā tasmādvikopaśca babhūva saḥ .. 6.69.10 ..
5.69.d:
तर्पिताः पितरश्चैव रुधिरेण महात्मना ..
प्रतिज्ञा पालिता तस्माद्विकोपश्च बभूव सः .. 6.69.10 ..
5.69.m: The ancestors were satisfied with blood by that great-souled one; / thus his vow was fulfilled, and he became free from anger.

5.69.s:
ekaviṃśatime prāpte tataśca pitṛtarpaṇe ..
aśarīrā'bhavadvāṇī khasthā pitṛsamudbhavā .. 11 ..
5.69.d:
एकविंशतिमे प्राप्ते ततश्च पितृतर्पणे ..
अशरीराऽभवद्वाणी खस्था पितृसमुद्भवा .. 11 ..
5.69.m: When the twenty-first ancestor-tarpaṇa was reached, / a bodiless voice arising from the ancestors spoke from the sky:

5.69.s:
rāmarāma mahābhāga tyajaitatkarma garhitam ..
vayaṃ te tuṣṭimāpannāḥ svavākyaparipāla nāt .. 12 ..
5.69.d:
रामराम महाभाग त्यजैतत्कर्म गर्हितम् ..
वयं ते तुष्टिमापन्नाः स्ववाक्यपरिपाल नात् .. 12 ..
5.69.m: 'Rāma, O fortunate Rāma! Desist from this despicable deed. / We are satisfied with you because of the fulfillment of your vow.

5.69.s:
yattvayā vihitaṃ karma naitadanyaḥ kariṣyati ..
na kṛtaṃ kenacitpūrvaṃ pitṛvairasamudbhavam .. 13 ..
5.69.d:
यत्त्वया विहितं कर्म नैतदन्यः करिष्यति ..
न कृतं केनचित्पूर्वं पितृवैरसमुद्भवम् .. 13 ..
5.69.m: The deed that was done by you no one else will do; / nor has such a deed arising from enmity over a father ever been done by anyone before.

5.69.s:
tasmāttuṣṭā vayaṃ vatsa dāsyāmaścitta vāṃchitam.
prārthayasva drutaṃ tasmāddurlabhaṃ tridaśairapi..14..
5.69.d:
तस्मात्तुष्टा वयं वत्स दास्यामश्चित्त वांछितम्.
प्रार्थयस्व द्रुतं तस्माद्दुर्लभं त्रिदशैरपि..14..
5.69.m: Therefore, my child, we are pleased and will grant your heart's desire. / Therefore, ask quickly for something even difficult for the thirty [gods] to attain.'

5.69.s:
rāma uvāca.
pitaro yadi tuṣṭā me yacchaṃti yadi vāṃchitam.
tasmāttīrthamidaṃ puṇyaṃ mannāmnā lokaviśrutam.
raktadoṣavinirmuktaṃ sevitaṃ varatāpasaiḥ..15..
5.69.d:
राम उवाच.
पितरो यदि तुष्टा मे यच्छंति यदि वांछितम्.
तस्मात्तीर्थमिदं पुण्यं मन्नाम्ना लोकविश्रुतम्.
रक्तदोषविनिर्मुक्तं सेवितं वरतापसैः..15..
5.69.m: Rāma said: / 'If the ancestors are pleased with me and grant my desire, / then let this sacred ford be known in the world by my name, / freed from the defect of blood, and frequented by the best ascetics.'

5.69.s:
pitara ūcuḥ.
pitṛtarpaṇajā gartā tvayā yeyaṃ vinirmitā.
rāmahrada iti khyātiṃ prayāsyati jagattraye .. 16 ..
5.69.d:
पितर ऊचुः.
पितृतर्पणजा गर्ता त्वया येयं विनिर्मिता.
रामह्रद इति ख्यातिं प्रयास्यति जगत्त्रये .. 16 ..
5.69.m: The ancestors said: / 'This pit born of the tarpaṇa for the ancestors, which was constructed by you, / shall attain renown throughout the three worlds as Rāmahrada.

5.69.s:
yatra bhaktiyutā lokāstarpayiṣyaṃti vai pitṝn ..
te'śvamedhaphalaṃ prāpya prayāsyaṃti parāṃ gatim...17..
5.69.d:
यत्र भक्तियुता लोकास्तर्पयिष्यंति वै पितॄन् ..
तेऽश्वमेधफलं प्राप्य प्रयास्यंति परां गतिम्...17..
5.69.m: Where people filled with devotion shall make tarpaṇa offerings to the ancestors, / they will obtain the fruit of an aśvamedha and reach the supreme state.

5.69.s:
kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ māsi bhādrapade naraḥ..
kariṣyati ca yaḥ śrāddhaṃ bhaktyā śastrahatasya ca...18..
5.69.d:
कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दश्यां मासि भाद्रपदे नरः..
करिष्यति च यः श्राद्धं भक्त्या शस्त्रहतस्य च...18..
5.69.m: Whatever person performs a śrāddha with devotion on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight / in the month of Bhādrapada for someone slain by weapons,

5.69.s:
api pretatvamāpannaṃ narake vā samāśritam..
uddhariṣyati sa pretamapi pāpasamanvitam...19..
5.69.d:
अपि प्रेतत्वमापन्नं नरके वा समाश्रितम्..
उद्धरिष्यति स प्रेतमपि पापसमन्वितम्...19..
5.69.m: he will deliver that deceased spirit, even if it has become a pretahood, / or has resorted to hell, or is tainted with sin.'

5.69.s:
sūta uvāca..
evamuktvā tu rāmaṃ te viremustadanaṃtaram..
rāmo'pi ca tapastepe tatraiva krodhavarjitaḥ..6.69.20..
5.69.d:
सूत उवाच..
एवमुक्त्वा तु रामं ते विरेमुस्तदनंतरम्..
रामोऽपि च तपस्तेपे तत्रैव क्रोधवर्जितः..6.69.20..
5.69.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus to Rāma, they fell silent thereafter; / and Rāma too performed austerities right there, free from anger.

5.69.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena tatra śastrahatasya ca..
tasmindine prakartavyaṃ śrāddhaṃ śraddhāsamanvitaiḥ..21...
5.69.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन तत्र शस्त्रहतस्य च..
तस्मिन्दिने प्रकर्तव्यं श्राद्धं श्रद्धासमन्वितैः..21...
5.69.m: Therefore, on that day, with every effort, a śrāddha should be performed / by the faithful for anyone slain by weapons.

5.69.s:
upasarga mṛtānāṃ ca sarpāgniviṣabandhanaiḥ..
tatra muktipradaṃ śrāddhaṃ dine tasminnudāhṛtam..22..
5.69.d:
उपसर्ग मृतानां च सर्पाग्निविषबन्धनैः..
तत्र मुक्तिप्रदं श्राद्धं दिने तस्मिन्नुदाहृतम्..22..
5.69.m: For those who died by affliction—by snakes, fire, poison, or hanging— / a śrāddha on that day is declared to bestow liberation.

5.69.s:
yaḥ pitṝṃstarpayettatra pretapakṣe jalairapi..
sa teṣāmanṛṇo bhūtvā pitṛloke mahīyate..23..
5.69.d:
यः पितॄंस्तर्पयेत्तत्र प्रेतपक्षे जलैरपि..
स तेषामनृणो भूत्वा पितृलोके महीयते..23..
5.69.m: Whoever satisfies the ancestors there with waters during the fortnight of the departed / becomes free of debt to them and is glorified in the ancestral world.

5.69.s:
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ rāmahradasamudbhavam..
māhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvapātakanāśanam..24..
5.69.d:
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं रामह्रदसमुद्भवम्..
माहात्म्यं ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठाः सर्वपातकनाशनम्..24..
5.69.m: All this māhātmya arising from Rāmahrada has been recounted to you, / O best of brahmins; it destroys all sins.

5.69.s:
śrāddhakāle naro bhaktyā yaścaitatpaṭhati svayam..
sa gayāśrāddhajaṃ kṛtsnaṃ phalamāpnotyasaṃśayam..25..
5.69.d:
श्राद्धकाले नरो भक्त्या यश्चैतत्पठति स्वयम्..
स गयाश्राद्धजं कृत्स्नं फलमाप्नोत्यसंशयम्..25..
5.69.m: A person who himself recites this with devotion at the time of a śrāddha / undoubtedly obtains the entire fruit born of a śrāddha at Gayā.

5.69.s:
parvakāle 'thavā prāpte paṭhedbrāhmaṇasaṃnidhau..
pitṛmedhasya yajñasya sa phalaṃ labhate 'khilam..26..
5.69.d:
पर्वकाले ऽथवा प्राप्ते पठेद्ब्राह्मणसंनिधौ..
पितृमेधस्य यज्ञस्य स फलं लभते ऽखिलम्..26..
5.69.m: Or when a sacred time has arrived, if he reads it in the presence of brahmins, / he obtains the entire fruit of a pitṛmedha sacrifice. // 26

5.69.s:
śṛṇuyādvāpi yo bhaktyā kīrtyamānamidaṃ naraḥ..
sautrāmaṇau kṛte kṛtsnaṃ phalamāpnotyasaṃśayam..27..
5.69.d:
शृणुयाद्वापि यो भक्त्या कीर्त्यमानमिदं नरः..
सौत्रामणौ कृते कृत्स्नं फलमाप्नोत्यसंशयम्..27..
5.69.m: Or whatever man listens with devotion to this being recited / obtains the entire fruit of a Sautrāmaṇī [sacrifice] that has been performed, without doubt. // 27

5.69.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryā saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye rāmahradotpattivṛttāntavarṇanaṃnāmaikonasaptatitamo' dhyāyaḥ .. 69 .. .. dha ..
5.69.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्या संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये रामह्रदोत्पत्तिवृत्तान्तवर्णनंनामैकोनसप्ततितमो' ध्यायः .. 69 .. .. ध ..
5.69.m: Thus ends the sixty-ninth chapter, entitled “Description of the Origin of Rāmahrada”, in the māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara kṣetra, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] in the venerable Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.70.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tathānyāpi ca tatrāsti śaktiḥ pāpapraṇāśinī ..
kārtikeyena nirmuktā hatvā vai tārakaṃ raṇe .. 1 ..
5.70.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तथान्यापि च तत्रास्ति शक्तिः पापप्रणाशिनी ..
कार्तिकेयेन निर्मुक्ता हत्वा वै तारकं रणे .. 1 ..
5.70.m: Sūta said: / Likewise, there is also another śakti [spear] there that destroys sin, / released by Kārtikeya after slaying Tāraka in battle. // 1

5.70.s:
tathāsti sumahatkuṇḍaṃ svacchodakasamāvṛtam ..
tenaiva nirmitaṃ tatra yaḥ snātvā tāṃ prapūjayet ..
sa pāpānmucyate sadya ājanmamaraṇāṃti kāt .. 2 ..
5.70.d:
तथास्ति सुमहत्कुण्डं स्वच्छोदकसमावृतम् ..
तेनैव निर्मितं तत्र यः स्नात्वा तां प्रपूजयेत् ..
स पापान्मुच्यते सद्य आजन्ममरणांति कात् .. 2 ..
5.70.m: Likewise, there is a very large pool filled with clear water, / created right there by him; whoever bathes [in it] and worships her [the śakti] / is immediately freed from sin committed from birth until death. // 2

5.70.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
kasminkāle vinirmuktā sā śaktistena no vada ..
kimarthaṃ svāminā tatra kiṃprabhāvā vada svayam .. .. 3 ..
5.70.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
कस्मिन्काले विनिर्मुक्ता सा शक्तिस्तेन नो वद ..
किमर्थं स्वामिना तत्र किंप्रभावा वद स्वयम् .. .. 3 ..
5.70.m: The seers said: / At what time was that spear released by him? Tell us. / For what purpose [was it cast] there by the lord? What is its power? Tell [us] yourself. // 3

5.70.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
purāsīttārakonāma dānavo'tibalānvitaḥ ..
hiraṇyākṣasya dāyādastrailokyasya bhayāvahaḥ .. 4 ..
5.70.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
पुरासीत्तारकोनाम दानवोऽतिबलान्वितः ..
हिरण्याक्षस्य दायादस्त्रैलोक्यस्य भयावहः .. 4 ..
5.70.m: Sūta said: / Formerly, there was a dānava named Tāraka, endowed with immense strength, / an heir of Hiraṇyākṣa, who caused terror to the three worlds. // 4

5.70.s:
sa jñātvā janakaṃ dhvastaṃ viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā ..
tapastepe tatastīvraṃ gokarṇaṃ prāpya parvatam .. 5 ..
5.70.d:
स ज्ञात्वा जनकं ध्वस्तं विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना ..
तपस्तेपे ततस्तीव्रं गोकर्णं प्राप्य पर्वतम् .. 5 ..
5.70.m: Knowing that his father had been destroyed by the mighty Viṣṇu, / he then went to Mount Gokarṇa and performed severe austerity. // 5

5.70.s:
yāvadvarṣasahasrāṃtaṃ śīrṇaparṇā śanaḥ sthitaḥ..
dhyāyamāno mahādevaṃ kāyena manasā girā..6..
5.70.d:
यावद्वर्षसहस्रांतं शीर्णपर्णा शनः स्थितः..
ध्यायमानो महादेवं कायेन मनसा गिरा..6..
5.70.m: For up to a thousand years he remained, feeding on withered leaves, / meditating on Mahādeva with body, mind, and speech, // 6

5.70.s:
varupūjopahāraiśca naivedyairvividhaistataḥ..
tato varṣasahasrāṃte sa daityo duḥkhasaṃyutaḥ .. 7 ..
5.70.d:
वरुपूजोपहारैश्च नैवेद्यैर्विविधैस्ततः..
ततो वर्षसहस्रांते स दैत्यो दुःखसंयुतः .. 7 ..
5.70.m: and then with various offerings, gifts of worship, and food oblations. / Then, at the end of the thousand years, that daitya, filled with grief, // 7

5.70.s:
jñātvā rudramasaṃtuṣṭaṃ tato raudraṃ tapo'karot ..
viniṣkṛttyātmamāṃsāni juhotisma hutāśane .. 8 ..
5.70.d:
ज्ञात्वा रुद्रमसंतुष्टं ततो रौद्रं तपोऽकरोत् ..
विनिष्कृत्त्यात्ममांसानि जुहोतिस्म हुताशने .. 8 ..
5.70.m: knowing Rudra to be ungratified, performed terrible austerity: / cutting off his own flesh, he offered it into the fire. // 8

5.70.s:
tatastuṣṭo mahādevo vṛṣārūḍha umāpatiḥ ..
sarvaireva gaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ tasya saṃdarśanaṃ yayau .. 9 ..
5.70.d:
ततस्तुष्टो महादेवो वृषारूढ उमापतिः ..
सर्वैरेव गणैः सार्धं तस्य संदर्शनं ययौ .. 9 ..
5.70.m: Gratified by that, Mahādeva, the lord of Umā mounted on the bull, / went to appear before him together with all his gaṇas. // 9

5.70.s:
tatra provāca saṃhṛṣṭastāranādena nādayan ..
diśaḥ sarvā mahādevo harṣa gadgadayā girā .. 6.70.10 ..
5.70.d:
तत्र प्रोवाच संहृष्टस्तारनादेन नादयन् ..
दिशः सर्वा महादेवो हर्ष गद्गदया गिरा .. 6.70.10 ..
5.70.m: There, delighted, making all the directions resound / with a loud sound, Mahādeva spoke with a voice faltering with joy: // 10

5.70.s:
bhobhostāraka tuṣṭo'smi sāhasaṃ medṛśaṃ kuru ..
prārthayasva mano'bhīṣṭaṃ yena te pradadāmyaham .. 11 ..
5.70.d:
भोभोस्तारक तुष्टोऽस्मि साहसं मेदृशं कुरु ..
प्रार्थयस्व मनोऽभीष्टं येन ते प्रददाम्यहम् .. 11 ..
5.70.m: “Hail, hail, Tāraka! I am pleased; do [not] perform such reckless daring! / Request your heart’s desire, so that I may grant it to you.” // 11

5.70.s:
.. tāraka uvāca ..
ajeyaḥ sarvadevānāṃ tvatprasādādahaṃ vibho ..
yathā bhavāmi saṃgrāme tvāṃ vihāya tathā kuru .. 12 ..
5.70.d:
.. तारक उवाच ..
अजेयः सर्वदेवानां त्वत्प्रसादादहं विभो ..
यथा भवामि संग्रामे त्वां विहाय तथा कुरु .. 12 ..
5.70.m: Tāraka said: / “O lord, by your favor, act in such a way that in battle / I may be unconquerable by all the gods, leaving you aside.” // 12

5.70.s:
.. bhagavānuvāca .. ..
matprasādādasaṃdigdhaṃ sarvametadbhaviṣyati ..
tvayā yatprārthitaṃ daitya tvameko balavāniha .. 13 ..
5.70.d:
.. भगवानुवाच .. ..
मत्प्रसादादसंदिग्धं सर्वमेतद्भविष्यति ..
त्वया यत्प्रार्थितं दैत्य त्वमेको बलवानिह .. 13 ..
5.70.m: The Lord said: / “By my favor, all this will come to pass beyond doubt, / as requested by you, O daitya; you alone shall be strong here.” // 13

5.70.s:
evamuktvā mahādevaḥ svameva bhavanaṃ gataḥ ..
tārakaścāpi saṃhṛṣṭastathaivanija mandiram .. 14 ..
5.70.d:
एवमुक्त्वा महादेवः स्वमेव भवनं गतः ..
तारकश्चापि संहृष्टस्तथैवनिज मन्दिरम् .. 14 ..
5.70.m: Having spoken thus, Mahādeva went to his own abode, / and Tāraka too, delighted, went likewise to his own palace. // 14

5.70.s:
tato dānavasainyena mahatā parivāritaḥ ..
gataḥ śakrapurīṃ yoddhuṃ vikhyātāmamarāvatīm .. 15 ..
5.70.d:
ततो दानवसैन्येन महता परिवारितः ..
गतः शक्रपुरीं योद्धुं विख्याताममरावतीम् .. 15 ..
5.70.m: Then, surrounded by a vast army of dānavas, / he set out to fight towards Indra’s city, the renowned Amarāvatī. // 15

5.70.s:
athābhavanmahāyuddhaṃ devānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha ..
yāvadvarṣasahasrāṃte mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam .. 16 ..
5.70.d:
अथाभवन्महायुद्धं देवानां दानवैः सह ..
यावद्वर्षसहस्रांते मृत्युं कृत्वा निवर्तनम् .. 16 ..
5.70.m: Then a great battle took place between the gods and the dānavas, / ending only with death, turning back at the close of a thousand years. // 16

5.70.s:
tatrābhavatkṣayo nityaṃ devānāṃ raṇamūrdhani ..
vijayo dānavānāṃ ca prasādācchūlapā ṇinaḥ .. 17 ..
5.70.d:
तत्राभवत्क्षयो नित्यं देवानां रणमूर्धनि ..
विजयो दानवानां च प्रसादाच्छूलपा णिनः .. 17 ..
5.70.m: There, the destruction of the gods occurred constantly at the forefront of the battle, / while the dānavas were victorious, by the grace of the wielder of the trident. // 17

5.70.s:
tataścakrurupāyāṃste vijayāya divaukasaḥ ..
varmāṇi suvicitrāṇi yantrāṇi parikhāstathā .. 18 ..
5.70.d:
ततश्चक्रुरुपायांस्ते विजयाय दिवौकसः ..
वर्माणि सुविचित्राणि यन्त्राणि परिखास्तथा .. 18 ..
5.70.m: Then those dwellers of heaven devised means for victory: / diverse armors, war machines, and trenches, // 18

5.70.s:
anyānyapi śarīrasya rakṣaṇārthaṃ prayatnataḥ ..
tathaiva yodhamukhyānāṃ viśeṣāddvijasattamāḥ .. 19 ..
5.70.d:
अन्यान्यपि शरीरस्य रक्षणार्थं प्रयत्नतः ..
तथैव योधमुख्यानां विशेषाद्द्विजसत्तमाः .. 19 ..
5.70.m: and others too, diligently made to protect the body, / especially for the foremost of warriors, O best of brahmins! // 19
